articles.title: Aussie captain denies claims of 2018 'sandpaper' plot
articles.excerpt: Australia's cricket captain Pat Cummins has again denied any involvement in the plot to use sandpaper on the ball in…
articles.fullText:
Australia's cricket captain Pat Cummins has again denied any involvement in the plot to use sandpaper on the ball in a test match against South Africa in 2018.

At a press conference in Sydney on Friday, he described the allegations in ex-teammate Usman Khawaja's autobiography as "utter nonsense".

Khawaja said last weekend that all the players in the team at Newlands knew about the plot, triggering calls for a new investigation into the incident.

"When he says we all knew, if by that he means that we knew sandpaper was going out in the field, he's 100 percent wrong. I've said that consistently for the last eight years," Cummins said.

"I did not know that was happening, but I think Usman actually says things that are actually far more serious than that. He says that I and others were architects of a scheme to ball tamper with sandpaper. That's complete and utter nonsense."

Cummins also took exception to Pakistan-born Khawaja's contention in the book that the colour of his skin and background had prevented him from becoming Australia captain.

"I think of all the things that I've read this week, I think that's actually the most serious," he said. "Him saying that if you're Australian captain, you have to be a certain skin colour, I couldn't disagree with that statement any more."

Steve Smith and David Warner, the then Australia captain and vice-captain, were banned by Cricket Australia from elite cricket for a year for their roles in the ball-tampering.

Warner on Monday said he backed Khawaja's version of events as "100 percent accurate".

"There's quite a few different accounts here, so they've got two accounts," said Cummins. "There's 11 players in that room, so that means there's nine other guys who I think it's appropriate you give an equal amount of weighting to their story as well."

Opening batter Cameron Bancroft, who brought a piece of sandpaper onto the field, received a nine-month suspension for his part in the ball-tampering.

Khawaja and Warner have also been critical of the Cricket Australia investigation in 2018 that found the three punished players solely responsible for the plot.

Earlier this week, the head of Cricket Australia ruled out opening another investigation into the incident.

Edited by Aaron Tam

articles.title: Housing Authority eases way for families, resales
articles.excerpt: The Housing Authority approved two measures to assist people in purchasing subsidised sale flats on Friday. This included a government…
articles.fullText:
The Housing Authority approved two measures to assist people in purchasing subsidised sale flats on Friday.

This included a government proposal aimed at further facilitating families with newborns to buy their own homes.

Starting with the next Home Ownership Scheme sale exercise, the maximum mortgage loan-to-value ratio for white form family applicants with newborns will be raised from 90 to 95 percent.

The authority said all families with children aged three or below by the application deadline could benefit from the new arrangement.

It would also relax the resale restriction period on subsidised flats that were first put up for sale between 2022 and 2025 from 15 years to 10 years.

“These two new measures will help more families move up the housing ladder while also promoting the turnover of subsidised sale flats, providing comprehensive assistance to members of the public to achieve home ownership,” a spokesman for the authority said.

Edited by Aaron Tam

articles.title: Bitter pill for rivals as Eli Lilly scores China first
articles.excerpt: China has approved its first orally administered GLP-1 weight-loss drug, permitting Eli Lilly to sell its orforglipron pill in a…
articles.fullText:
China has approved its first orally administered GLP-1 weight-loss drug, permitting Eli Lilly to sell its orforglipron pill in a market where 630 million adults could be overweight or obese by 2050.

GLP-1 drugs aid weight loss by mimicking a natural gut hormone that suppresses appetite and regulates blood sugar levels.

The medication has soared in popularity in recent years, with drugmakers now competing to release pills as an alternative to existing injection treatments.

The National Medical Products Administration said on Thursday it had approved US-based pharmaceutical giant Eli Lilly's pills, marketed as "Muyouda", to treat obese or overweight adults with at least one weight-related condition.

The American company's once-daily pills were approved in the United States in April.

It has beaten competitors such as Danish firm Novo Nordisk – which makes Wegovy – to be the first to gain approval for an oral version of the medicine in China.

GLP-1 injections from Eli Lilly, Novo Nordisk, and domestic firm Innovent are already widely available in the country.

The Chinese market for weight-loss treatments is growing rapidly.

The number of obese or overweight adults in China could reach 630 million by 2050, according to a 2025 study published in The Lancet.

The National Health Commission has warned that 65 percent of China's population will be obese or overweight by 2030. (AFP)

Edited by Aaron Tam

articles.title: W Kowloon losses a time-lag problem: Bernard Chan
articles.excerpt: Heavy losses incurred by the West Kowloon Cultural District Authority are the result of a "time-lag problem" that ensues when…
articles.fullText:
Heavy losses incurred by the West Kowloon Cultural District Authority are the result of a "time-lag problem" that ensues when cultural venues have opened but the commercial developments meant to support them have not yet been built, its chairman said.

Speaking on RTHK's "On Broadcast Drive" programme, Bernard Chan said the district already has two museums and two performance venues up and running but the revenue flowing in from the box office and venue hirings is far from enough to break even.

"No cultural facility anywhere in the world can balance its books solely on tickets, venue hire or dining," he said, pointing out that other cities are backed by all manner of subsidies.

"Some have very high taxes, so many funds and companies are very willing to donate because it reduces their tax bill. In places like Europe, most of it is government subsidies."

The commercial part of the development is only just getting under way, he said, with some projects due to open next year and others several years later, while spending on them has already begun – which is why the losses look so daunting.

Chan said he was determined to turn West Kowloon into both a cultural and a commercial centre as artistic undertakings need financial support to be sustainable, and the two have to coexist.

He noted that the national 15th Five-Year Plan supports Hong Kong deepening its development as a centre for cultural and artistic exchanges between the nation and the world.

In this regard, Chan said, the city's prolonged contact with the West lets it present Chinese culture in a way that audiences, including overseas visitors, can understand, making it a unique strength of the city.

Edited by Aaron Tam

articles.title: Microsoft service disruption hits businesses, govts
articles.excerpt: Microsoft services such as Outlook and Teams were disrupted for about 10 hours on Thursday as the tech giant struggled…
articles.fullText:
Microsoft services such as Outlook and Teams were disrupted for about 10 hours on Thursday as the tech giant struggled to fix issues with some servers, hitting businesses and government agencies globally that use the popular platforms.

In its latest update, Microsoft said efforts to improve serviceability were not progressing as expected.

"We’re identifying alternate workstreams that can be applied to increase capacity in the face of sustained traffic management imbalances," it said.

Downdetector, which tracks outages by collating status reports from a number of sources, showed more than 25,000 reports of Outlook problems in the US at 9.30pm EST, or 10.30am local time. It also showed outages for several Microsoft services in the Asia-Pacific region, including India, Australia and Japan.

At its peak, Downdetector showed more than 130,000 reports of Outlook problems in the US around 1pm EST on Thursday.

In a service health notice, Microsoft said features of Microsoft 365 services that depended on Exchange Online and email were affected, while elements that did not rely on Exchange Online remained functional. Exchange Online is the company's cloud-based messaging platform that delivers email, calendar, contacts, and tasks. (Reuters)

Edited by Aaron Tam

articles.title: CE hails the SAR's 41 medals at Asian Para Games
articles.excerpt: Chief Executive John Lee on Friday praised SAR athletes at a homecoming ceremony for the Hong Kong, China delegation, after…
articles.fullText:
Chief Executive John Lee on Friday praised SAR athletes at a homecoming ceremony for the Hong Kong, China delegation, after they won 41 medals at the fifth Asian Para Games.

The team won three gold, 14 silver and 24 bronze medals. More than 150 people were sent, including 80 elite athletes and more than 70 support staff, to compete in 10 sports.

Lee said the boccia team recorded its best-ever result, taking two gold, three silver and three bronze medals, while swimmers took one gold, three silvers and five bronzes. The table tennis team also collected 15 medals.

"You have proven through your actions that true strength lies in persistence and the courage to break through," he said.

"On the competitive stage of the Asian Para Games, you have shown the resilient Hong Kong spirit. Through your actions, you have told Hong Kong's story well and added glory to the nation's sporting development."

The government is providing about HK$71 million in 2026-27 for the Hong Kong Sports Institute to train elite athletes with disabilities, more than 50 percent higher than five years ago, Lee said.

He added that the government will continue to provide systematic training and all-round support for elite athletes with disabilities through the institute – including training venues, professional coaches, and sports science and sports medicine services, with the aim to help them keep improving and win more honours for Hong Kong, China on the international stage.

Edited by Aaron Tam

articles.title: 'Govt to check more items during lift inspections'
articles.excerpt: Secretary for Development Bernadette Linn on Friday said the government would improve its acceptance-inspection regime for lifts. Her remarks came…
articles.fullText:
Secretary for Development Bernadette Linn on Friday said the government would improve its acceptance-inspection regime for lifts.

Her remarks came after authorities found that 720 lifts installed by Taizoom Elevator were missing mandatory fire resisting door frame components.

Speaking at a special meeting of the Legislative Council’s Panel on Development, Linn said the Electrical and Mechanical Services Department’s on-site inspections only focused on safety-related components, which should be further expanded to cover other parts.

“For other areas, such as the lift’s smoothness and its door frame, we have to admit that under the current mechanism, we mainly relied on registered lift engineers to carry out inspection without checking on-site,” she said.

“We think this is a point that must be adjusted in the acceptance-inspection regime in the future.”

Linn said she hoped the department could finish reviewing its mechanism by the end of the year.

“We don’t want to bring in an independent third party every time a problem arises in the regulatory authorities, because it would only result in layer upon layer of regulation while increasing the costs,” she said.

“Also, don’t forget that even a third party itself might fail to comply with the rules.”

Linn said the authorities would conduct spot checks when non-governmental personnel are involved in building works and impose punishments that carry a deterrent effect.

Edited by Aaron Tam

articles.title: Lawmakers concerned over QMH lift faults
articles.excerpt: Lawmakers voiced concern on Friday over the seriousness of the lift faults at Queen Mary Hospital's new clinical block, after…
articles.fullText:
Lawmakers voiced concern on Friday over the seriousness of the lift faults at Queen Mary Hospital's new clinical block, after Secretary for Development Bernadette Linn reported the investigation findings to a special meeting of the Legislative Council.

Linn told the development panel meeting the main contractor and subcontractor bear the main responsibility for the lift faults, while those responsible for monitoring, including government staff, also had failings in management and supervision.

"First, the main contractor and the lift subcontractor carried out inaccurate works, the workmanship was poor, and follow-up was sloppy," she said.

"Second, the inspection, testing and approval plan drawn up by the main contractor for the lift installation had omissions, and neither the professionals it hired nor Architectural Services Department staff followed them up."

She said the problem was not systemic as the works-supervision system itself is in place, but the project team did not carry it out properly, so the shortcoming was in execution.

DAB vice chairman Chan Hok-fung described the case as a "perfect storm".

"Every link fell a little short, and these shortcomings came together, leading to such a big incident," he said.

"You can say it is the system or you can say it is the people, but after reading the report the system is actually sound – there are three layers of approval, three layers of structure, and many people were watching throughout the process. So why could it not be done? I agree that the problem with people is very serious, and that is the most critical point in this case."

Liberal Party vice chairman Lee Chun-keung called some aspects of the incidents unbelievable.

"It now looks very much like a deliberate, chain-by-chain cover-up – but in the end, they couldn't wrap fire with paper. By the time it reached the Hospital Authority, the whole thing had gone wrong," he said.

"Why the Hospital Authority was still allowed to use the lifts? Some of these things are truly unbelievable and baffling."

Linn said the investigation found that staff from the Architectural Services Department were negligent when issuing the completion certificate, while there were also shortcomings in how the Electrical and Mechanical Services Department issues lift use permits.

Faults among the 28 lifts have delayed the building's full opening.

Edited by Aaron Tam

articles.title: Xi Jinping to chair Apec summit in Shenzhen
articles.excerpt: President Xi Jinping will chair the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Apec economic leaders' meeting and deliver remarks, the Ministry of…

President Xi Jinping will chair the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Apec economic leaders' meeting and deliver remarks, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs announced on Friday.

The meeting will be held in Shenzhen from November 18 to 19 under the theme "Building an Asia-Pacific Community to Prosper Together", a spokesperson said.

The Apec CEO summit will be held in Shenzhen from November 17 to 18 under the theme "To Prosper and Win the Future Together", the spokesperson said, adding that Xi will attend the opening ceremony and deliver a keynote speech.

He will hold a welcome banquet for participating leaders and representatives, and hold bilateral meetings with foreign leaders on the sidelines of the meeting, the spokesperson added. (Xinhua)

articles.title: Japanese PM to attend Shenzhen Apec meeting
articles.excerpt: Tokyo on Friday said Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi will visit China next week for the first time since she…
articles.fullText:
Tokyo on Friday said Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi will visit China next week for the first time since she took office, attending an Asia-Pacific summit in Shenzhen.

"Prime Minister Takaichi is scheduled to visit the Philippines and China from November 16 to 19 to attend Asean-related summit meetings and the Apec summit," said deputy chief cabinet secretary Masanao Ozaki.

At Apec, Ozaki said Takaichi – who became Japan's leader last October – would discuss issues such as "trade and investment, regional economic integration, economic and energy resilience, the digital economy ... and present Japan's position on these matters".

Before the Shenzhen trip she will head to Manila for a meeting of the 11-nation Association of Southeast Asian Nations.

Ozaki said a Quad meeting – which would include the leaders of Australia, India, Japan and the United States – is being arranged on the sidelines of the Asean meeting.

In a policy address last month, Takaichi called China an "important neighbour" and pledged to build a stable relationship. (AFP)

Stocks in Asia were on steadier footing on Friday after a turbulent week dominated by revelations of extramarital affairs involving Nvidia cofounder Jensen Huang that culminated in his resignation, a blow to the global AI boom he helped advance.

In Hong Kong, the benchmark Hang Seng Index started the day down 136 points, or 0.57 percent, at 23,871.

The China Enterprises Index slipped 46 points, or 0.57 percent, to 8,010 while the tech index edged down 13 points, or 0.35 percent, to 3,918.

The Shenzhen Component Index rose 38 points, or 0.34 percent, to 11,236 while the ChiNext Index climbed 15 points, or 0.64 percent, higher to 2,525.

Jon Zauderer, Citi's head of specialist sales and a TMT specialist, said competitors such as AMD, Arista and Broadcom could benefit from the Nvidia fallout.

articles.title: Crow-Armstrong, Alvarez earn MLB MVP honours
articles.excerpt: Chicago Cubs outfielder Pete Crow-Armstrong was named baseball's National League Most Valuable Player on Thursday, ending Los Angeles Dodgers star…
articles.fullText:
Chicago Cubs outfielder Pete Crow-Armstrong was named baseball's National League Most Valuable Player on Thursday, ending Los Angeles Dodgers star Shohei Ohtani's two-year reign.

The 24-year old was a unanimous selection ahead of Ohtani and Brice Turang of the World Series champion Milwaukee Brewers, earning all 30 first-place votes from a panel of the Baseball Writers' Association of America.

Houston Astros slugger Yordan Alvarez won the American League award, becoming the fourth Cuban to earn MVP honours.

Crow-Armstrong delivered one of the best all-around seasons in MLB history, tying Kyle Schwarber for the MLB lead in home runs with 45 and finishing second in the National League in stolen bases with 41.

He became the seventh player in history with a 40-40 season and joined Ohtani (2024) and Alfonso Soriano (2006) as the only players to have at least 45 home runs, 40 steals and 30 doubles in one year.

Crow-Armstrong played 162 games, piling up 107 runs-batted-in with 83 walks and scoring 119 runs.

He joins an illustrious list of Cubs players to win the award, including Ernie Banks in 1958 and 1959, Ryne Sandberg in 1984, Sammy Sosa in 1998 and, most recently Kris Bryant in 2016.

"I don't even know where to put myself in all that," said Crow-Armstrong, flanked by family as he spoke on the MLB Network's award presentation ceremony.

"I've been so lucky to be around such great Cubs and even more than that just really big people and names in the game of baseball.

"I'm happy to be able to carry on their legacy," he said. (AFP)

Edited by Aaron Tam

articles.title: Filipino fishermen urge Manila to defend territorial waters – their fishing grounds
articles.excerpt: Philippines will look to finalize South China Sea code of conduct during ASEAN meetings in Manila next week.
articles.fullText:
MANILA, Philippines - Ahead of two major international meetings for Manila next week, fishermen in the Philippines are urging their government to press the international community on territorial disputes with Beijing in the South China Sea that they say are responsible for a decreased catch, the fishermen told Radio Free Asia.
The Philippines will host a summit of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations, or ASEAN, from Nov. 15 to 17. In addition to the 10 leaders of the regional economic bloc, leaders of other global partners are also attending, including U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese Premier Li Qiang.
Immediately after the ASEAN Summit, many of the same leaders will fly to Shenzhen, China for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation, or APEC, leaders meetings.
The meetings come at a crucial time for the Philippines, as analysts say Manila will try to rally the international community to their side in disputes over waters in the South China Sea that are claimed both by the Philippines and China. Manila hopes to finalize a “code of conduct” governing actions in the sea region at the ASEAN summit, but analysts and observers are doubtful that the agreement will be completely hammered out before it ends.
China’s incursions into the Philippines’ exclusive economic zone are directly to blame for dwindling fish catches, Joey Marabe, a Filipino fisherman, told RFA.
“We used to fish in Scarborough Shoal with other fishermen from other nations,” he said. But when China began claiming it as their own, “we were accused of stealing resources and fish in our own seas.”
Rising Tension
Scarborough Shoal is a rich fishing ground within the EEZ of the Philippines, but has been under Chinese control since 2012. Marabe hails from the coastal town of Masinloc, about 150 kilometers (94 miles) northwest of Manila. The shoal lies due west.
China claims territory within its “nine-dash line,” which essentially encircles the entirety of the South China Sea, including the shoal.
After escalating tensions that ultimately led to a standoff over the shoal in 2012, Manila took the dispute to the international arbitration court. The court issued a ruling in 2016 that invalidated the nine-dash line, but Beijing rejects the ruling and still maintains control of the shoal.
Marabe, a leader in the fishermen’s rights group Pamalakaya, said that a code of conduct for the South China Sea between China and ASEAN must put the welfare of fishermen first, and the regional bloc must be willing to work together to ensure that China follows through on its commitments.
“The government must also be prepared to fight and defend our sovereign rights,” he said.
Filipinos need to put their domestic political differences aside and speak to China with a singular voice to get a code of conduct done, Rodrigo Laudit, a fisherman from the coastal community of Las Piñas in Manila, told RFA. He said fishermen would be the most affected by the code, or lack thereof.
The Philippine Department of Foreign Affairs “should lead all agencies of the government that are dealing with WPS in this,” he said, using the abbreviation of the West Philippine Sea, the part of the South China Sea inside the Philippines’ EEZ. “Above the dwindling catch, it is Filipinos’ sovereignty that is at stake here.”
But diplomacy can only go so far, Dindo Manhit, president of the Manila-based Stratbase Institute, told RFA.
“It cannot replace transparency and public accountability,” he said, warning against diplomatic considerations that could potentially weaken defense of sovereignty.
Manhit’s comments are in response to recent debates over how Manila should walk the tightrope of responding to Beijing’s encroachments into its EEZ while also maintaining good relations with China, a major economic partner.
Discretion and diplomacy can work, but they “must never be used to suppress scrutiny or silence officials on matters of core national interests,” he said. “Exposing coercion and unlawful maritime activities is a lawful defense of our rights,” he stressed.
Deescalation?
For now, both sides appear to be dialing down the tension to avoid a further deterioration of diplomacy, recognizing the potential impact of tough talk on bilateral ties and economic discussions, analysts said.
Both sides must also be careful not to undermine their respective diplomatic meetings, Lucio Pitlo, a policy and security analyst based in Manila, told RFA. In October, Beijing sent its lowest-level delegation to a defense ministers’ meeting held in the central Philippine island of Cebu.
Philippines Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro, center, delivers his opening remarks during the 13th ASEAN Defence Ministers' Meeting-Plus (ADMM-Plus) in Cebu, Philippines on Oct. 29, 2026.
(Eloisa Lopez/AFP) “One important goal is to avoid a possible snub or low-level delegation attending each other’s event, which may not look well for the host and affect the enthusiasm of other regional leaders attending the meetings,” he said.
Pitlo, who heads the Philippine Association of Chinese Studies, noted that the foreign ministers of both countries had also recently agreed during a “much-needed phone call to stabilize ties ahead of the back-to-back regional summits.”
During the phone conversation, China’s Foreign Minister Wang Yi told his Filipino counterpart Theresa Lazaro that bilateral relations were facing “malicious disruptions” from unnamed Filipino officials who have allegedly smeared China. He called on the Philippines to boost restraint over the officials and send “a rational and unified voice on its policy toward China.”
“For the Philippines, avoiding the economic fall-out from heated verbal and social media exchanges between some Philippine security officials and the Chinese embassy” means that “President Marcos has had to encourage officials to be more cautious about their language, recognizing its potential diplomatic impact,” said Pitlo.
Edited by Eugene Whong.

articles.title: Exclusive: US-sanctioned Jinan Supercomputing Center still gets Nvidia AI products
articles.excerpt: Despite export control restrictions, Chinese research facilities continue acquiring advanced chips.
articles.fullText:
Read a version of this story in Mandarin
As Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Thursday announced his resignation amidst a scandal over an alleged extramarital affair that may have been a Chinese spy plot targeting him, a Radio Free Asia investigation revealed that sanctioned entities in China were able to get ahold of the company’s AI chips despite U.S. restrictions.
The U.S. government will continue to investigate Jensen Huang’s involvement with Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, a former executive at Singapore cloud data center company Megaspeed, who is suspected of collecting intelligence for Beijing and assisting Chinese clients in obtaining restricted chips.
This “AI industry earthquake” triggered by news of Huang’s departure has attracted intense outside attention. After the U.S. restricted direct exports of certain Nvidia products to China starting in 2022 , can sanctioned Chinese institutions still obtain Nvidia computing equipment through overseas cloud services or domestic suppliers?
RFA’s investigation of Chinese government procurement data revealed that Nvidia’s RTX 5090 graphics cards and DGX Spark products appeared in a winning bid announcement for an AI equipment procurement project this year by China’s Shandong Computing Center, also known as the National Supercomputing Center Jinan.
However, according to U.S. government regulations, even if the aforementioned products can enter China, they cannot be purchased or used by the Jinan Center because it appears on a list of export control entities .
On June 17, 2026, the China Government Procurement Network ( web archive ) published a procurement result announcement. The procured item was the “Edge Intelligent Computing Team AI Workstation and Graphics Card Procurement Project.” The winning bidder was Qiyuan Jiasu (Tianjin) Technology Co., Ltd., with a winning bid price of RMB 148,500 (US$22,000). The product list in the procurement document contained two items: “RTX5090” and “DGXSPark”, while the brand column indicated “Yixin,” a brand operated by Qiyuan Jiasu.
Information from China Government Procurement Network shows that the Shandong Computing Center, which is subject to U.S. chip sanctions, was still soliciting bids for Nvidia high-end products as of June 2026.
(Government Procurement Network; RFA graphic) Information from China Government Procurement Network shows that the Shandong Computing Center, which is subject to US chip sanctions, was still soliciting bids for Nvidia high-end products as of June 2026. (Screenshot from China Government Procurement Network; RFA graphic)
“RTX 5090” is a graphics card from Nvidia that uses the Blackwell architecture and is equipped with 32GB GDDR7 memory; DGX Spark is a desktop AI computing system launched by Nvidia equipped with the GB10 Grace Blackwell Superchip.
The procurement quantity for this tender only indicated “one batch” without explicitly specifying how many RTX 5090 graphics cards or how many DGX Spark units were included in “one batch.”
Different restrictions on selling two products into China
RFA further checked Nvidia product categories and U.S. export control regulations, finding that rules for selling the two products into China’s general market are not the same.
The RTX 5090 graphics card has a standard version and a “special edition” tailored specifically for the Chinese market. The former falls under advanced computing products controlled by the U.S. which cannot be shipped to China without an applicable license. The special versions of the card have model numbers RTX 5090 D and RTX 5090 D v2. However, the Jinan Center’s procurement announcement only listed “RTX 5090,” making it impossible to confirm whether the purchase was for the original version or the China special edition.
The DGX Spark, a desktop AI computer equipped with the GB10 Grace Blackwell Superchip, is listed on Nvidia’s official Chinese website with purchasing channels in China. Therefore, the DGX Spark can indeed be sold in China’s general market.
However, availability in China’s general market does not allow for unrestricted sale to entities like the National Supercomputing Center Jinan.
Purchasing party identified by U.S. in 2021
The Shandong Computing Center was established in 1976 and is affiliated with Qilu University of Technology; the National Supercomputing Center Jinan was established in 2011, and both currently belong to the same institutional framework.
The U.S. Department of Commerce’s entity list explicitly listed “Shandong Computing Center” as an alias for “National Supercomputing Center Jinan.” The center was placed on the list in April 2021, prior to the broad export restrictions on advanced computing chips to China that the U.S. began implementing in 2022.
The U.S. Department of Commerce stated at the time that seven Chinese supercomputing and chip institutions, including Jinan, Shenzhen, Wuxi, and Zhengzhou, had procured U.S.-origin items to support Chinese military units, military modernization, and weapons of mass destruction programs. The U.S. determined that these activities were contrary to U.S. national security and foreign policy interests.
After being added to the entity list , exporting, re-exporting, or transferring items subject to the U.S. Export Administration Regulations, or EAR, within China to the Jinan Center in principle requires a license from the U.S. Department of Commerce, and without a license, it is subject to a presumption of denial. These restrictions target specific transaction counterparties and are not limited to prohibiting high-end AI chips purchased by general Chinese customers.
Chris Tseng, an overseas researcher at Taiwan’s Research Institute for Democracy, Society and Emerging Technology, told RFA that items regulated under the U.S. Export Administration Regulations theoretically require review by the Bureau of Industry and Security, or BIS under the U.S. Department of Commerce whenever shipped to an entity on the entity list, even for items with looser control standards.
Tseng added that U.S. export controls travel with the item itself, so even if these two products were shipped to legitimate Chinese or third-country distributors, a license is still required to transfer them to a controlled entity like the Shandong Computing Center.
“The broader issue is that current controls still rely heavily on corporate self-compliance,” he said. “Whether it’s Nvidia tracking customers and end-users, or Chinese and other potential third-country distributors failing to comply with U.S. export rules upon transfer,” both present challenges.
Bloomberg News reported that in inventory verification reports submitted by Nvidia to the U.S. government, it was revealed that approximately 50,000 AI chips sold to Megaspeed were underreported. The uncounted chips were valued at billions of dollars, raising concerns that chips leaked illicitly into China via Southeast Asia.
Ties between the winning supplier and sanctioned distributor
The winning bidder in the deal in RFA’s investigation, Qiyuan Jiasu (Tianjin) Technology Co., Ltd., shares multiple noteworthy similarities with Sitonholy (Tianjin) Technology, a Chinese company that was once a major Nvidia partner and was later sanctioned by the U.S.
Radio Free Asia reviewed public data for both companies and found that they both describe themselves on their webpages as “a leading artificial intelligence infrastructure solution provider,” using identical text.
The homepages of Sitonholy (Tianjin) Technology, top, and Qiyuan Jiasu use the same phrase “a leading artificial intelligence infrastructure solution provider" (in red box).
(Sitonholy (Tianjin) Technology, Qiyuan Jiasu; RFA graphic) Both companies also set their production bases in Wuqing, Tianjin, and marketing offices in Shangdi, Beijing. The partner clients listed on both companies’ websites are also completely identical, including Tsinghua University, Peking University, Beijing Institute of Technology, as well as the CAS Institute of Computing Technology, Institute of Automation, Institute of Mechanics, Institute of Remote Sensing, and Institute of Information Engineering; even the phrasing and order listed by both companies are identical.
The partner clients of Qiyuan Jiasu, top, and Sitonholy (Tianjin) Technology are identical, listed in the same order (red box).
(Qiyuan Jiasu, Sitonholy (Tianjin) Technology; RFA graphic) “Their business registration and website introductions are almost identical,” a commentator familiar with China’s AI industry told RFA in an interview, stating that this strongly raises suspicion that Qiyuan Jiasu might be a new entity taking over part of Sitonholy (Tianjin) Technology’s business after it was sanctioned by the US. “This is one company operating under two banners; Qiyuan Jiasu may be a new shell used after Sitonholy (Tianjin) Technology was placed on the Entity List.”
Public data shows that Sitonholy (Tianjin) Technology had been an NPN authorized partner of Nvidia since 2015 and was described as an Nvidia Elite Partner, DGX Series official authorized value-added reseller, and Tesla Series core partner. Reports from the Tianjin Economic-Technological Development Area government in 2023 also confirmed its status as an Nvidia Elite Partner.
However, the U.S. Department of Commerce placed Sitonholy (Tianjin) Technology on the Entity List sanctions on April 11, 2024, citing that the company acquired US-origin items to support Chinese military modernization.
Li Houchen, a Japan-based current affairs and economic columnist, remarked during an interview that if Qiyuan Jiasu indeed inherited Sitonholy (Tianjin) Technology’s original operations, Nvidia would need to investigate the sales and ultimate flow of related products. However, current public information can only verify that the company profiles, client lists, and operational locations of the two companies overlap heavily, with no direct evidence yet proving both belong to the same ultimate beneficial ownership system.
Experts: Export controls have exploitable loopholes
Sylvia Chen, an economic security policy analyst at DSET who previously worked in sanctions and export control legal advisory, told RFA that under current U.S. regulations, third-party enterprises can’t first purchase controlled products and then export or transfer them within China to the National Supercomputing Center Jinan. If carrying out such resales, third-party enterprises may likewise bear legal liability for violating export control regulations.
However, Chen pointed out that practical enforcement faces staffing constraints. Currently, the U.S. Department of Commerce’s Bureau of Industry and Security has only one export control officer stationed in Beijing responsible for end-use and end-user verification; worldwide, there are only 15 such officers.
From a corporate compliance perspective, suppliers including Nvidia have an obligation to conduct “Know Your Customer” (KYC) procedures. Once suspicious “red flags” appear in a transaction, the enterprise should further verify the product’s end-use, end-user, and destination. If relevant doubts remain unresolved and the company proceeds with the transaction, it may be deemed that Nvidia “should have known” that illegal diversion of the product existed, thereby assuming corresponding liability.
Chen noted that current rules do not mandate companies to continuously track chip locations, though such technology already exists. Public reports indicate Nvidia has offered an opt-in tracking software feature to Blackwell chip customers.
Currently, provisions related to the “Chips Security Act” have been incorporated into amendments proposed by the Senate for the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027, or NDAA. The final text of the FY2027 NDAA will still be confirmed whether the relevant clauses of the Chips Security Act will be retained and ultimately passed into law.
Chen believes that even if the bill fails to pass, the next Congress controlled by Democrats may still reintroduce stricter export control measures.
Tseng told RFA that current supervision mainly consists of three levels: pre-shipment investigation of customers and end-users by Nvidia; post-shipment end-use checks by BIS export control officers; and self-directed spot checks by enterprises regarding product destination, or enhancing oversight via location verification tech under discussion in the Chips Security Act. Additionally, in specific cases, inter-country intelligence sharing and law enforcement cooperation can be used to trace product destinations.
China needs dual-use supercomputing technology
The Jinan Municipal Government’s 2019 publication “Opinions on Accelerating the Industrialization Development of Supercomputing” requires the National Supercomputing Center Jinan to lead the establishment of a collaborative innovation alliance, and to “establish and improve a mechanism for mutual access and sharing of military and civilian technology resources,” perform “joint key research on dual-use supercomputing technology,” and promote the industrialization of related technology.
The same policy document also listed medical health, artificial intelligence, new materials, agricultural disaster prevention, and smart manufacturing as supercomputing application fields. This demonstrates that the Jinan Center simultaneously undertakes civilian scientific research, industrial development, and military-civilian dual-use technology missions, though it cannot be assumed based on this that the equipment procured this time will be used directly for military projects.
Government procurement records show that the Jinan Center conducted this procurement through a Chinese domestic supplier. Public information shows that the winning company, Qiyuan Jiasu, deals in GPU servers, Nvidia graphics cards, and high-performance computing equipment, and has supplied servers to Chinese universities and research institutions in the past.
RFA sent an email to Nvidia asking whether it was aware of this procurement, whether the relevant products obtained applicable U.S. export licenses, and whether it will launch an investigation into this case. No response was received prior to press time.
RFA also inquired with Qiyuan Jiasu and the Shandong Computing Center to learn whether this procurement project had received US authorization or involved smuggling issues; no response has been received yet.
Translation reviewed by Ruo Shui, edited by Charlie Dharapak and Eugene Whong in English.

articles.title: Warriors' Curry out two weeks with abdominal tear
articles.excerpt: Golden State Warriors star Stephen Curry will miss at least two weeks after suffering an oblique abdominal tear, the NBA…
articles.fullText:
Golden State Warriors star Stephen Curry will miss at least two weeks after suffering an oblique abdominal tear, the NBA team said on Thursday.

Curry exited Wednesday's loss to the Houston Rockets midway through the first quarter. He appeared to be in some discomfort just minutes into the game.

After the Warriors' 115-108 defeat, coach Steve Kerr said Curry had told him the injury was not one he had experienced before.

"Concern is high," Kerr said, and an MRI scan revealed the tear.

Curry, 38, has been playing at an elite level this season, averaging 27.8 points per game with 3.7 rebounds and 3.9 assists.

He is shooting a career-high 45.7 percent from three-point range and was instrumental in an eight-game Warriors winning streak that ended on Wednesday.

The injury is another blow to a Golden State squad already without Jimmy Butler and Moses Moody, both recovering from knee injuries.

Curry, a four-time NBA champion and two-time Most Valuable Player, missed 39 games last season, 27 of them with a nagging knee injury. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Scaloni to stay on as Argentina coach until 2030
articles.excerpt: Lionel Scaloni on Thursday agreed to stay on as coach of Argentina's national football team until after the 2030 World…
articles.fullText:
Lionel Scaloni on Thursday agreed to stay on as coach of Argentina's national football team until after the 2030 World Cup, ending the doubts that had been swirling since this year's World Cup final defeat.

Scaloni's decision to renew his contract was announced by Argentine Football Association president Claudio Tapia at a press conference with the 48-year-old manager.

Scaloni, who took the Albiceleste to victory at the 2022 tournament in Qatar, told reporters he was as enthusiastic as "on day one".

"A new project begins now," he said a month after Lionel Messi, the team's leading light for 20 years, bowed out of international football.

Tapia said that Scaloni would be the Argentina manager with the most World Cups under his belt by the time his contract ended.

Scaloni had cast doubt on his future with the team after Argentina's 1-0 defeat by Spain in a bad-tempered July 19 World Cup final in New Jersey.

He has been coach for eight years, taking over in September 2018, after a traumatic World Cup in Russia, where Argentina were eliminated in the round of 16.

Scaloni took over one of the most prestigious jobs in football without any prior experience and built the team into one widely considered the best in Argentine history.

Besides the 2022 World Cup he coached Argentina to two Copa America titles, in 2021 and 2024.

He now faces the task of taking the team forward without his 39-year-old talisman Messi.

"What must remain is this team spirit, this feeling of unity among the players and the people," he said after losing the final to Spain. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Spain maintain perfect Nations League record
articles.excerpt: Alex Baena scored from the spot and Marc Pubill added another seconds from time as Spain beat ten-men Czech Republic…
articles.fullText:
Alex Baena scored from the spot and Marc Pubill added another seconds from time as Spain beat ten-men Czech Republic 2-0 in the Nations League in Prague on Thursday.

The win leaves Spain unbeaten in 44 competitive games in a row, including five wins in as many Nations League games this season.

Spain, who already secured a quarter-final berth before travelling to Prague, will face England in Madrid on Sunday in their final Group A3 game.

Baena scored on 39 minutes after a VAR check revealed Czech midfielder Lukas Ambros had handled the ball inside the box.

The Atletico Madrid winger blasted his spot kick past Matej Kovar who touched the ball but failed to clear it.

Czech captain Ladislav Krejci was sent off in the 69th minute after bringing down second-half substitute Roberto Fernandez on a counter-attack.

It was a deja-vu for the Wolverhampton defender who also got a red card at the end of Spain's 3-1 home win over the Czechs last month.

Pubill, another substitute, beat Eindhoven goalkeeper Kovar with a clinical low shot deep into stoppage time after robbing Tomas Soucek.

"I want to appreciate the work of the entire team," said Spain coach Luis de la Fuente.

"It was a difficult game against an energetic team with an aggressive style. We had moments when it cost us a lot of energy to control the game."

De la Fuentes missed Lamine Yamal, Dani Olmo, Rodri and Eric Garcia with injuries while Mikel Oyarzabal was sidelined with flu.

Spain got off to a slow start on the chilly evening but never really let the hosts get close throughout the first half.

They gradually stepped up their pressure, often confining the Czechs to their box and looking for chances.

Fabian Ruiz hit the post with a curling right-footer three minutes from halftime, while Dean Huijsen's header found Kovar's arms.

Yeremy Pino, replacing Yamal on the right flank, saw his goal overturned by VAR for offside just two minutes into the second half.

The Czechs showed higher spirits after the break, but David Zima tipped the ball over the bar from close range and Adam Hlozek's glancing header landed on the top of the crossbar.

The Czechs lost momentum after the red card, but Baena had two efforts cleared by Kovar and Fernandez saw his shot stopped by Kovar and then hit the post.

"The score could have been higher but we struggled with the finish," said de la Fuente.

He added Yamal and Oyarzabal would rejoin the team ahead of the England game.

"We have good news, they will join us tomorrow and will be ready for the England game," he continued. "If everything goes well, they can both play 90 minutes."

The hosts, led by de la Fuente's long-time collaborator Santi Denia, have lost all their Nations League games this season.

They are next travelling to Croatia for a game they need to win to stay in the top tier of the competition for the next edition. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Kane hungry for more after England caps record
articles.excerpt: Harry Kane pledged he would play for England "for as long as I can" after winning a record 126th cap…
articles.fullText:
Harry Kane pledged he would play for England "for as long as I can" after winning a record 126th cap against Croatia on Thursday.

The England captain scored from the penalty spot as Thomas Tuchel's team won 2-1 at Wembley to guarantee a spot in the Nations League quarter-finals in March.

The 33-year-old, who won the Ballon d'Or last month, moved clear of former goalkeeper Peter Shilton, who won 125 caps during his long career.

Shilton was part of a pre-match presentation to honour the Three Lions captain, along with Football Association patron Prince William.

A giant banner was raised before kick-off with a picture of Kane and the words "England's Finest".

The skipper, who showed off his Ballon d'Or trophy to the Wembley crowd before the match, described the occasion as "incredible".

"I was trying to play it cool, I was trying to not smile too much, not give away too much emotion," he said. "Obviously I try to stay focused on the job."

Kane added: "I don't know if any of this has sunk in, to be honest with you, maybe in the winter break when I've got a couple of weeks off.

"I'll be on the beach somewhere and we'll try and reflect on everything that I've achieved, because these ones are probably the biggest in my career, without a doubt."

The Bayern Munich forward said he was inspired by the example set by Croatia veteran Luka Modric, 41, who came on as a late substitute at Wembley.

"That inspires me to push the limits," he said. "Like with him, I think you just keep going to see how far your body takes you, your mentality takes you.

"Everyone's journey is different, for sure, but... as long as I feel like I can help the national team, as long as I feel like I'm performing at the highest level, then I'll be here for as long as I can.

"Whether that's until I'm 40 or not, we'll have to wait and see, but right now, yeah, I'm enjoying every moment." (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Israeli strike on Gaza hospital deadliest since poll
articles.excerpt: Israeli fire killed 10 people in Gaza on Thursday, six of whom died in the bombing of Nasser hospital in…
articles.fullText:
Israeli fire killed 10 people in Gaza on Thursday, six of whom died in the bombing of Nasser hospital in south Gaza early in the day, health officials said, the deadliest single strike since Israel's elections last month.

The Israeli military confirmed the attack on the medical complex, saying they targeted "a senior Hamas terrorist and additional terrorists from Hamas's military wing" who it said were operating from the hospital, which it has long accused the Palestinian Islamist movement of using to shelter militants.

Hamas has denied this, and both parties frequently accuse each other of violating the terms of a US-backed ceasefire agreement that took effect in October 2025.

Nasser Hospital, located in Khan Younis, confirmed the six deaths in a statement, while a doctor there said that nearly 30 were wounded.

Goher Rahbour, a British surgeon volunteering at the Hospital, said that Palestinian doctor Rizeq Abu Sheikh, with whom he had conducted a surgery on Wednesday evening, was among those killed in the strike on Thursday.

"I was on my phone just doing a bit of reading and the strike occurred just after midnight. It was very loud, very quick. The building shook, there was a lot of smoke that came up," Rahbour said.

Gaza's civil defence agency said the bodies from the strike had been recovered from the targeted building, which a medical source said was the surgery ward of Nasser Hospital, a sprawling medical complex in the southern city of Khan Younis.

The rescue agency reported four more deaths on Thursday. One person was killed by "Israeli gunfire" near the al-Bureij camp and another in an "Israeli drone strike" targeting a vehicle near Deir al-Balah, both in central Gaza.

Two more people were killed in an Israeli strike on a vehicle near Gaza City's al-Shifa hospital, bringing Thursday's total death toll to 10.

Israel's military said it struck a militant in Deir al-Balah and another in Gaza City, but denied that the second strike took place near al-Shifa Hospital.

Israel is currently led by a caretaker government under Benjamin Netanyahu following an inconclusive election, with opposition bloc head Gadi Eisenkot officially tasked with forming a new administration.

Netanyahu, who has held power on-and-off for nearly 20 years and has led Israel throughout the war in Gaza, has played up security threats to the country throughout the election period and called for a unity government.

More than 1,600 Palestinians have been killed since the start of the ceasefire, according to the Gaza Ministry of Health, which operates under Hamas authority and whose figures are considered reliable by the United Nations.

During the same period, the Israeli military has reported the loss of seven soldiers, as well as one civilian contractor. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Trump tells Vance to focus on corruption, not Iran
articles.excerpt: US President Donald Trump said on Thursday the US does not need a deal with Iran and directed Vice President…
articles.fullText:
US President Donald Trump said on Thursday the US does not need a deal with Iran and directed Vice President JD Vance, who has played a role in efforts to resolve the war, to focus "his complete and total attention" on alleged crime and corruption in Democratic-run cities and states.

Trump's directive came a day after the Wall Street Journal reported that Vance was considering face-to-face peace talks with an Iranian security official and a week after the vice president blamed the costly war with Iran for Republicans' midterm elections drubbing.

"We don’t need a deal with Iran. Those days have long since passed. We've got their money, Hundreds of Billions of Dollars, and we've got their Strait!" Trump wrote on social media, referring to the Strait of Hormuz.

Trump had suggested in recent weeks that Iran would be more willing to strike a deal in the eight-month conflict after the US elections, but his administration this week signalled it believes its blockade and economic sanctions against Iran are working, meaning neither a military escalation nor diplomacy is needed.

The US military is imposing a blockade on Iranian ports, while attempting to secure safe passage for international shipping through the vital Strait of Hormuz.

Iran's military said on Thursday four oil tankers were hit by explosions after they ignored Iranian warnings.

Vance's office did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Vance, long seen as sceptical of the war the US and Israel launched on Iran in February, led talks with Iranian officials in Pakistan in April that produced a June memorandum of understanding that paused the war but broke down within weeks.

Iranian state media said late last month Tehran had received a letter from Vance seeking renewed talks with Washington. Trump said he had not directed his vice president to make the outreach.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Tuesday after talks with US allies in Paris that Iran's demands for a potential deal were "absurd," citing its demand for reparations for the war, and said Trump would not sign a bad deal.

The Wall Street Journal reported on Wednesday that Vance was considering meeting with a senior Iranian security official, a move that would have put Vance at the centre of peace negotiations. Reuters has not confirmed the potential talks.

Vance, who is viewed as a leading contender for the 2028 Republican presidential nomination, distanced himself from the war last week after Republicans' midterm election rout by Democrats.

The vice president blamed the costs of the Iran war in part for the party's losses. He also said an earlier recommendation to end the war was "sound advice."

Trump responded to Vance's position by defending the war as necessary to stop Iran from obtaining a nuclear weapon.

In his social media post, Trump said he had asked Vance to focus instead on a domestic issue the president previously put in his portfolio: leading an effort targeting alleged fraud in Democratic-run cities and states throughout the US.

"Our Budget could be quickly BALANCED with the correction of this large-scale criminal activity. CORRUPTION is in the Democrat Leadership’s blood!" Trump wrote on Thursday. (Reuters)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Europe to join Ukraine peace talks
articles.excerpt: Ukraine President Volodymyr Zelenskiy on Thursday welcomed news that Europeans would be present at the next round of US-brokered peace…
articles.fullText:
Ukraine President Volodymyr Zelenskiy on Thursday welcomed news that Europeans would be present at the next round of US-brokered peace talks with Russia, and expressed hope that the agenda would include steps towards ceasefires and de-escalating the conflict.

Zelenskiy, speaking after talks with US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, said it was important that the peace process had restarted, following the first talks in nine months earlier this week in Abu Dhabi.

"It's important that everything is unblocked," Zelenskiy said, after meeting the US envoys whilst in Dublin to attend a European summit.

"We decided that we will work on an agenda about any kind of de-escalation, some kind of ceasefires... I hope that we will have such agenda. Yes, this is important."

Earlier on Thursday, Witkoff had announced a new round of talks would take place soon involving European officials, after he and Kushner met with Russian leader Vladimir Putin in Moscow.

"The Europeans will join at the next meeting, which we consider to be a very important moment because they are our partners and it's important to us that they take part," Witkoff told Russian state TV.

Putin said Moscow had always been open to talking to the EU about Ukraine, but signalled serious outstanding differences.

"As far as the Europeans are concerned, we have never been opposed to engaging in dialogue with Europe, and we have never broken off that dialogue. It was they who broke off the dialogue with the Russian Federation," he said.

He then warned that the European idea of sending Western troops into Ukraine once a peace deal was concluded would trigger a resumption of the war because Russia would see that as a threat to its own security.

"We would very much like you, gentlemen, and the US administration as a whole, to work with your European allies so that they can finally make up their minds as to what they want: peace or war in Ukraine," said Putin.

Putin has shown no signs of being ready to moderate his territorial demands, which include a buffer zone in parts of Ukraine which Russia has not formally claimed as its own.

He said on Thursday that what Russia considers as its state border should be the only meaningful demarcation point with Ukraine. (Reuters)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Tenant kills manager, shoots four in Washington
articles.excerpt: A disgruntled tenant shot dead his building manager and wounded four other people in an upscale neighbourhood of Washington on…
articles.fullText:
A disgruntled tenant shot dead his building manager and wounded four other people in an upscale neighbourhood of Washington on Thursday before killing himself, police said.

The shooting, which occurred about a mile north of the White House, sparked a massive police response in the nation's capital with dozens of law enforcement vehicles racing to the scene and police helicopters hovering overhead.

Jeffery Carroll, Washington's interim police chief, told reporters that the gunman, identified as Matt Lambert, 55, had been involved in an ongoing dispute over maintenance with the condominium association for the building where he owned an apartment.

Lambert, an emergency medicine physician, fatally shot the building manager in a gym attached to the complex, located in the Logan Circle neighbourhood, and then barricaded himself in his seventh-floor unit, Carroll said.

He then opened fire from his balcony on people below, wounding four. One of the wounded was in critical condition while the others did not have life-threatening injuries.

Lambert fired at least twice at police through his apartment door before shooting himself, Carroll said. He was pronounced dead at the scene.

Carroll said Lambert had taken legal action against the homeowners association of the condominium complex where he lived over what he considered to be a lack of maintenance of the building.

An X feed reportedly linked to Lambert titled @OfMiceandMold is a litany of complaints about mould and water damage. The final post, described as a "manifesto," is an engineering report detailing problems with his apartment.

Washington Mayor Muriel Bowser denounced what she described as a "senseless act of gun violence."

The shooting occurred during the busy morning rush hour, snarling traffic as police closed off streets around the area and evacuated residents.

The Washington Sun quoted a member of the VIDA Fitness gym as saying that he was on a treadmill at the workout facility when the shooting began.

Michael Carney said he heard a "pop" and then saw someone on the gym floor who had been shot in the head.

"Everyone was kind of just hiding behind planters and stuff," Carney told The Sun.

The Logan Circle neighbourhood is one of the most expensive in Washington and is known for chic restaurants and nightlife spots. It also sits a short distance from a heavy concentration of foreign embassies. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Wall St down as Nvidia drop outweighs energy gains
articles.excerpt: US stocks closed lower on Thursday, as a drop in Nvidia shares after CEO Jensen Huang's exit outweighed gains in…
articles.fullText:
US stocks closed lower on Thursday, as a drop in Nvidia shares after CEO Jensen Huang's exit outweighed gains in energy shares.

The chip company's shares fell 4.3 percent but were well off the day's lowest level after earlier dropping nearly 12 percent. Retail investors bought Nvidia shares worth about US$111 million in the first half hour of trading, the biggest opening bid on record for the stock, according to data from Vanda Analytics.

The S&P 500 energy index rose 1.5 percent, its fourth straight session of gains, as the best-performing of the 11 major S&P sectors. Crude prices climbed after US President Donald Trump wrote on social media that the US did not need a deal with Iran.

Global AI-linked stocks fell and AI cloud firm Nebius tumbled 16.8 percent, its biggest daily percentage drop since July 1, after reporting its quarterly earnings and outlook. But Nvidia competitors such as Broadcom, Advanced Micro Devices and Alphabet each moved higher and were among the biggest boosts to the S&P 500.

Equities have been volatile in recent days. Sweeping Democratic victories in the US midterm elections have sparked investor concern about more AI regulation. Worries about Nvidia's leadership have also pressured one of the foundations of the current bull market. Nvidia tabbed Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress as interim CEO.

"Right now, the market is selling AI stocks and tech stocks and buying safe stuff, just like it did in the first halo trade in January and February of this year, but it will flip back," said Jed Ellerbroek, portfolio manager at Argent Capital Management in St Louis.

"That's the tug of war the market is doing right now. It's concerns about deceleration versus just pointing out that the absolute valuation and growth rates are still pretty compelling."

The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 189 points, or 0.4 percent, to 52,297, the S&P 500 lost 26 points, or 0.4 percent, to 7,592 and the Nasdaq Composite lost 100 points, or 0.4 percent, to 25,366.

Even with Huang's departure, some investors expect questions to persist about the future of AI companies with strong ties to Nvidia.

The company has backed several firms, including its own customers, through financing arrangements that face greater scrutiny after Huang's departure.

"Nvidia is the circular-funder-in-chief; they're the biggest by far at this point, and I assume that activity will moderate," said Ellerbroek.

The Philadelphia Semiconductor index declined 0.5 percent after surging 17.2 percent over the prior four sessions.

Along with Nebius, peer CoreWeave dropped 6.9 percent. Shares of data centre-related firms IREN and Applied Digital slumped 6.5 percent and 5.4 percent, respectively.

Investors are awaiting the release of the Producer Price Index on Friday, which will follow a hotter-than-expected consumer price reading earlier this week.

Markets are completely pricing in a December rate hike of at least 25 basis points by the Federal Reserve, with a 15 percent chance of a 50-basis-point increase, according to CME FedWatch.

Comments from multiple Fed officials earlier this week suggested the US central bank was open to a more aggressive path of rate hikes as price pressures worsen.

Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack said on Thursday she does not believe the central bank needs to shift to more aggressive rate hikes to combat inflation, while San Francisco Federal Reserve President Mary Daly said she thinks the central bank will likely need to raise interest rates further to deal with elevated inflation, but did not suggest any urgency. (Reuters)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Hegseth decorates soldier who rebuked him at Arlington
articles.excerpt: Pete Hegseth on Thursday awarded a medal to a US soldier who reprimanded the US defence chief and his entourage…
articles.fullText:
Pete Hegseth on Thursday awarded a medal to a US soldier who reprimanded the US defence chief and his entourage for laughing and talking near the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier the day before.

Hegseth "proudly awarded Specialist Thomas Iglesias the Joint Service Commendation Medal for the execution of his duties at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier on November 11, 2026," a Pentagon official said.

A post on Hegseth's official X account included photos showing him pinning the medal on the soldier's uniform and shaking his hand.

"We love soldiers. We love standards. Well done, Specialist," text accompanying the photos said.

The tomb, at Arlington National Cemetery near Washington, is a sacred burial place of American military personnel killed during World War I, World War II and the Korean War. It also includes an empty site for a Vietnam War soldier in honour of missing troops from that conflict.

Video on US networks and social media showed Hegseth and his entourage gathering to take photos on Wednesday at the tomb after a Veterans Day ceremony.

"All visitors will maintain an atmosphere of silence and respect at all times!" a US Army sentinel yelled loudly in response to audible laughter and chatter.

CNN identified the group taking photos on the steps near the tomb with Hegseth as his wife Jennifer, chief of staff Ricky Buria, deputy chief of staff Patrick Weaver and senior advisor Tami Radabaugh.

The tomb is patrolled at all times by soldiers who volunteer for the job and undergo "a strict selection process and intensive training," according to the cemetery's website. (AFP)

Edited by Robert Kemp

articles.title: Nvidia privately confirmed it could track chips to fight smuggling, even as industry publicly questioned feasibility
articles.excerpt: Representatives from Nvidia told Illinois representative Bill Foster that it would be technically possible to implement the anti-smuggling measures called…
articles.fullText:
Representatives from Nvidia told Illinois representative Bill Foster that it would be technically possible to implement the anti-smuggling measures called for in the Chip Security Act, Foster told MIT Technology Review in an interview on Thursday, even while an industry group claimed they were “potentially infeasible.” 

Foster, a Democrat who serves on the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, is a cosponsor of the act, which would introduce geotracking requirements to verify the location of advanced AI chips in order to prevent their smuggling to China. It is one of three chip-security bills under consideration for inclusion in the Senate’s National Defense Authorization Act, each of which is drawing renewed attention after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s resignation and reported affair with an alleged Chinese spy.

When the Chip Security Act was introduced, in May 2025, lawmakers said the technology to implement it existed, something Nvidia has not publicly confirmed. In March 2026, the Semiconductor Industry Association, of which Nvidia is a member, explicitly opposed the bill and wrote that its mandates for chip tracking were “new, untested, and potentially infeasible.” 

But privately, Nvidia representatives working with Foster told the lawmaker that the company could implement them. 

“They never put anything in writing,” Foster says, but during technical discussions on the possibility of such safeguards, their reaction was “yeah, of course we can do this.” This private acknowledgment to Foster goes further than anything Nvidia has previously made public. 

Other technology Nvidia has built for its customers suggests that the company can indeed offer accurate tracking of its chips’ locations. In December 2025, for example, it announced a new tool called Fleet Intelligence that would allow customers to monitor how its advanced chips were performing across different data center locations. In doing so, the tool could indicate which country chips were in, Nvidia confirmed to Reuters, but the company would not elaborate on whether this technology could be used to prevent smuggling. 

Nvidia did not respond to requests for comment or confirmation of Foster’s characterization.

In early October, when lawmakers were reportedly increasingly concerned about Nvidia’s role in smuggling, MIT Technology Review asked the company if Fleet Intelligence could be used to prevent the practice. It declined to answer directly, instead sending a statement: “Governments and media have found insignificant diversion of controlled US products—a drop in the bucket compared to the ocean of domestic compute China already has.”

The recent fallout at Nvidia involves a number of people and companies alleged to be involved in chip smuggling. Alice Huang, with whom Jensen Huang reportedly had an affair, runs Megaspeed, a Singaporean firm now under investigation for smuggling advanced GPUs to China. A US Commerce Department inquiry into the company was reportedly halted after invention by Nvidia. Megaspeed reportedly bought chips from Supermicro, a company that packages Nvidia’s chips onto servers.

The Chip Security Act as drafted would require a mechanism to track the locations of chips, either by inspections of facilities, attestations by companies, or ping-based location mechanisms. The ping-based technique, the hardest option to circumvent, would require the GPU to send a signal of its location when it comes online. In September, the Center for Security and Emerging Technology found it would be the most cost-effective option.

Foster said he did not ask Nvidia’s representatives why they weren’t voluntarily adopting such chip-tracking tools if they could technically do so.

But if the requirements of the bill pass as part of the Senate’s National Defense Authorization Act, the new tracking mechanisms would only tell investigators where the chips are, not offer a way to disconnect them if it’s revealed they have been smuggled. Foster told MIT Technology Review he intends to introduce new, stricter legislation in the new year that would offer a workaround. The new rule would require licenses to operate advanced GPUs, and before a GPU could connect, its valid license would need to be verified.

In the meantime, the controversy at Nvidia, Foster says, has fueled support among his colleagues for the rules in the bill: “There will be a lot of political pressure, in the wake of everything that’s happened, on the companies to actually do a very good job of the geographic validation of where the chip actually is.”

articles.title: PNG observers call for restraint from China and US over ‘wine bottle’ shell
articles.excerpt: The statements by Beijing and Washington undermine the jurisdiction of PNG authorities, observers said.
articles.fullText:
PORT MORESBY, Papua New Guinea – The U.S. and China should stop trying to push their own narratives and allow the Papua New Guinea Police to handle the case of an allegedly smuggled artillery shell found in a shipping container imported by a Chinese company, a senior communications expert from the Pacific country told Radio Free Asia.
Police last week confirmed that the shell seized on Oct. 29 was indeed a 130-millimeter round, contrary to the Chinese embassy’s claim on social media that it was merely a harmless wine bottle that was shaped like an artillery shell.

The U.S. Embassy disputed the claim on social media, saying that the U.S. military had “engaged” with the PNG Explosive Ordnance Disposal Unit, who determined that it was a Chinese-manufactured artillery projectile.
PNG police detained four Chinese men in connection with the incident.
But letting the U.S. or China influence public opinion through their statements undermines the PNG police and the country’s sovereignty, Joseph Ealedona, a former media executive and former president of Port Moresby Soccer Association, told RFA.
“It is a police investigation and only the PNG police will release details,” he said. “We Papua New Guineans do not come to your country and announce matters under police investigation.”

He called for restraint from the embassies of both countries.
“The Chinese and U.S. Embassies must respect our sovereignty and refrain from making public statements,” he said. “The matter is under active police investigation. It must not be used for geopolitical interests. We are friends to U.S. and China so this must be respected.”
‘A 21st century arms race’
The “wine bottle” shell is part of a “superpower arms race,” former diplomat Dominic Sengi wrote in a commentary published in local newspaper The National.
“PNG and the Pacific has become an increasingly important arena of strategic competition where superpowers come courting and subscribing nations in their spheres,” he wrote.

The smaller Pacific Islands, he said, have welcomed both because they feel like they stand to gain something when the larger powers compete.
“Come one, come all, invest in our country. Build our roads, finance our ports, train our police, support our defense forces. Establish diplomatic missions, bring your development programs – friends to all, enemies to none,” he wrote, describing what he called a “pragmatic, almost laissez-faire” approach to international relations.
“Laissez-faire diplomacy however becomes problematic when welcoming everyone means allowing everyone to pursue their strategic interests without sufficient national scrutiny.”
He said that Beijing and Washington’s competing explanations over the incident are themselves “instruments of political engagement.”
“Both countries speak the language of friendship and mutual respect,” he wrote. “Yet PNG must ask whether these declarations are always identical to the interests of our peoples.”
Papua New Guinea’s closing of Taiwan’s trade office in Port Moresby this month was described as puzzling from a diplomatic standpoint, experts told RFA, but it signals a coming expansion of its economic relationship with China.
Edited by Eugene Whong.

articles.title: Maritime Week to open on Sunday
articles.excerpt: Hong Kong Maritime Week (HKMW) 2026 - a flagship annual maritime event anticipated worldwide - will be held for seven…
articles.fullText:
Hong Kong Maritime Week (HKMW) 2026 - a flagship annual maritime event anticipated worldwide - will be held for seven consecutive days from Sunday, expected to attract over 18,000 participants to join its online and offline events.

The Transport & Logistics Bureau will also announce several important maritime-related deliverables during the week.

The HKMW is co-ordinated by the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government, organised by the Hong Kong Maritime & Port Development Board, and co-organised by the Hong Kong Shipowners Association and the Hong Kong Maritime Museum, with the Hong Kong Trade Development Council and Invest Hong Kong as partners.

Jointly hosted by more than 80 local, Chinese Mainland and overseas maritime organisations, there will be more than 60 events covering flagship forums, high-level seminars, industry exhibitions and business networking.

Policymakers, leaders of major international shipping organisations, business decision-makers, experts and industry elites from around the globe, including high-ranking government officials from Belt & Road countries will explore the latest development opportunities in the global maritime industry during the HKMW.

The National 15th Five-Year Plan Outline indicates clear support for Hong Kong in consolidating and enhancing its dual-hub status as an international maritime centre and an international aviation hub.

First held in 2016, HKMW has evolved over the years into a premier international event for the maritime, port and logistics sectors. The Government will announce the new batch of partner ports, and will sign a number of maritime-related memoranda of understanding at its 10th anniversary.

To heighten public awareness of Hong Kong's thriving maritime development, the bureau has partnered with Television Broadcasts (TVB) to produce a 10-episode promotional drama series Navigating to the Future. The series will be broadcast from next Monday to November 27, every Monday to Friday, across channels 81, 82 and 83.

An array of community and youth engagement programmes will also be rolled out, including a maritime-themed carnival set on November 21 and 22.

articles.title: Sha Tin site to be sold
