The Lands Department today announced that Sha Tin Town Lot No. 626, at the junction of Tai Chung Kiu Road and On Sum Street, in Shek Mun, will be sold by public tender.

The tender invitation for it, in the 2026-27 Land Sale List, will begin next Friday and close on December 18.

The lot is designated for non-industrial purposes, "excluding godown, hotel and petrol filling station".

It has a site area of about 8,015 sq m and its gross floor area will be between 29,816 sq m and 49,693 sq m.

Land sale documents will be available on the Lands Department’s website from next Friday.

articles.title: Subsidised flat measures enhanced
articles.excerpt: The Housing Authority’s Subsidised Housing Committee today approved two enhancement measures in relation to subsidised sale flats (SSFs), to help…
articles.fullText:
The Housing Authority’s Subsidised Housing Committee today approved two enhancement measures in relation to subsidised sale flats (SSFs), to help members of the public achieve home ownership.

One of the measures is lowering the home ownership threshold for families with newborns. Starting from the next Home Ownership Scheme (HOS) sale exercise, the maximum mortgage loan-to-value ratio for White Form family applicants with newborns will be raised from 90% to 95%, in line with that for Green Form applicants.

All families with children aged three or below at the HOS sale exercise application deadline will benefit from this measure.

The other approved measure is relaxing the alienation restriction period – the timeframe during which owners face strict rules on selling, letting, or assigning their properties – for SSFs first put up for sale between 2022 and 2025. The period will be shortened from 15 years to 10 years from the date of first assignment. This is to encourage more homeowners to pursue upward mobility along the housing ladder.

The authority said the two new measures will help more families move up the housing ladder while also promoting the SSF turnover.

articles.title: HK to set up new drug regulator
articles.excerpt: The Centre for Medical Products Regulation Bill was published today in the Government Gazette, establish statutory status for the Centre…
articles.fullText:
The Centre for Medical Products Regulation Bill was published today in the Government Gazette, establish statutory status for the Centre for Medical Products Regulation (CMPR) and to allow the regulatory framework for Chinese and Western medicines and medical devices to be unified in the future.

The bill will be introduced into the Legislative Council for first reading on November 25.

The bill includes three major proposals. First, to establish the CMPR as a body corporate to represent Hong Kong, China in international regulatory affairs concerning medical products and establish formal, long-term working relationships with leading regulatory authorities worldwide.

Second, to unify the regulatory framework, the bill proposes to build on existing legislation to transfer the relevant regulatory powers and functions concerning Chinese and Western medicine, currently vested in the Pharmacy and Poisons Board of Hong Kong, the Chinese Medicines Board of the Chinese Medicine Council of Hong Kong and their committees, as well as those relating to medical devices, after legislation in the future, to the Director of Health.

Third, to enhance the relevant supporting mechanisms and make necessary technical amendments.

Secretary for Health Prof Lo Chung-mau said the establishment of the CMPR marks a significant milestone in Hong Kong's regulatory reform of medical products.

He added that the Government will comprehensively and proactively align with the National 15th Five-Year Plan, fully leveraging Hong Kong's distinctive advantages of enjoying strong support nationally and being connected to the world under the “one country, two systems” principle.

“We will establish a proactive mechanism for the evaluation and approval of medical products, enabling advanced products to be introduced into Hong Kong more quickly for the benefit of patients and developing Hong Kong into an international health and medical innovation hub,” he said.

The health chief added that the Government will deepen collaboration with regulatory authorities around the world and pursue recognition from international authorities.

“Our long-term goal is to develop the CMPR into an internationally recognised regulatory authority for medical products."

Prof Lo emphasised that the Government is committed to providing a world-class and modern regulatory environment to accelerate the clinical application of innovative medical products while ensuring their safety, quality and efficacy, making good drugs and medical devices available for use in Hong Kong.

The Government will also support the emerging biomedicine industry in its research and development regarding innovative medical products, facilitating their introduction into Hong Kong and expansion into international markets, he said.

articles.title: Industry keen on HSK logistics
articles.excerpt: The invitation for expressions of interest (EOI) in the development of selected land parcels at the modern logistics cluster in…

The invitation for expressions of interest (EOI) in the development of selected land parcels at the modern logistics cluster in the Hung Shui Kiu/Ha Tsuen New Development Area (HSK Logistics Cluster) closed today, with 16 submissions received from developers, logistics operators, logistics industry associations and professional services providers.

The Government has reserved approximately 32 hectares of land at the Hung Shui Kiu/Ha Tsuen New Development Area of the Northern Metropolis for the development of a modern logistics cluster to meet long-term demand for logistics land.

Jointly issued by the Transport & Logistics Bureau and the Civil Engineering & Development Department on August 13, the invitation for EOI covers the first batch of five selected sites within the HSK Logistics Cluster. The initiative aims to gauge market interest, collect industry feedback on development requirements, and refine land disposal arrangements ahead of upcoming tender exercises.

The bureau will now analyse the submissions to help finalise the tender requirements and land disposal terms. Tenders for the first available sites are expected to be invited towards the end of 2027 at the earliest, with the relevant tender to be awarded in 2028.

articles.title: CE lauds HK’s Para Games athletes
articles.excerpt: Chief Executive John Lee today officiated at a Commendation Ceremony for the Hong Kong, China delegation to the 5th Asian…
articles.fullText:
Chief Executive John Lee today officiated at a Commendation Ceremony for the Hong Kong, China delegation to the 5th Asian Para Games.

He presented certificates of commendation to the Hong Kong athletes in recognition of their outstanding performance in the games.

Speaking at the ceremony, Mr Lee said the delegation had demonstrated Hong Kong's "persevering and never-give-up" spirit on at the games. He added that the athletes’ outstanding achievements were supported by the dedication and hard work of the coaching team and medical support staff.

The Chief Executive iterated that the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government is fully committed to supporting para sports and elite athletes. Since April 2025, the Government has raised direct financial support for all elite athletes, including para-athletes, by 8.3% across the board. A Senior Squad category has been introduced into the elite tier for para-athletes, improving their training pathway.

The Hong Kong, China delegation of 80 athletes participated in 10 events at the games, which were held from October 18 to 24.

The delegation won 41 medals – three gold, 14 silver and 24 bronze – and achieved Hong Kong's best-ever haul in boccia of two gold, three silver and three bronze medals.

articles.title: Rural polling dates published
articles.excerpt: The polling dates for the 2027 Rural Ordinary Election were published in the Government Gazette today. The Village Representative Election…
articles.fullText:
The polling dates for the 2027 Rural Ordinary Election were published in the Government Gazette today.

The Village Representative Election will be conducted on January 17, 2027, while the Kaifong Representative Election for Market Towns will be held on January 24, 2027. The nomination period will take place from November 24 to December 7.

The election covers 709 recognised villages with a total of 1,484 representative seats. These comprise 695 resident representative seats and 789 indigenous inhabitant representative seats. Separately, the market towns on Cheung Chau and Peng Chau will elect 39 and 17 neighbourhood (“kaifong”) representatives respectively.

​A notice specifying the polling date, time and polling station address will be issued to eligible electors at least 10 days before the polling day.

Call 2152 1521 or contact the relevant New Territories district office for enquiries.

articles.title: Economy rises 5.2% in Q3
articles.excerpt: (To watch the full press conference with sign language interpretation, click here .) Underpinned by a further pick-up in external…
articles.fullText:
(To watch the full press conference with sign language interpretation, click here .)

Underpinned by a further pick-up in external trade growth and solid domestic demand, Hong Kong's economy expanded strongly in the third quarter of 2026, with real gross domestic product (GDP) rising 5.2% year on year.

Presenting the Third Quarter Economic Report 2026 at a press conference today, Government Economist Irina Fan said that in the first three quarters, real GDP grew by 5.1% over a year earlier, which is the fastest pace in five years for the corresponding period.

Total goods exports surged 30.3% year on year in the third quarter, fueled by strong global demand for artificial intelligence-related electronics.

Domestically, private consumption rose 2.9% for its sixth consecutive quarter of growth.

Factoring in the results from the first three quarters and expectations of continued solid growth in the fourth, the full-year GDP growth forecast for 2026 has been revised up to 4.8%.

Looking ahead, Ms Fan said that, supported by robust global AI investment and related trade, Hong Kong's economy is poised for a strong full-year performance.

“Incoming data for entering the fourth quarter also points to sustained growth momentum. Domestic demand should stay resilient. However, uncertainty in the external environment persists, including those from geopolitical tensions, US monetary policy, and trade protectionist measures. So, all of these are worth closer monitoring.”

She noted that the overall inflation rate should remain moderate.

Taking into account inflation in the first three quarters, the forecasts for the underlying and headline consumer price inflation rates for 2026 have been revised down to 1.9% and 2.0% respectively.

articles.title: Contractor, govt depts blamed over QMH faulty lifts
articles.excerpt: The Development Bureau has identified deficiencies and shortcomings by the contractor, professionals and government departments in the installation of faulty…
articles.fullText:
The Development Bureau has identified deficiencies and shortcomings by the contractor, professionals and government departments in the installation of faulty lifts at Queen Mary Hospital's new clinical block.

Chief Executive John Lee ordered an investigation in September after most of the lifts in the 34-storey tower were sealed off.

In a report submitted to the Legislative Council on Thursday, the Development Bureau said all 28 lifts in the building experienced problems to varying degrees.

It said "verticality deviations" in the lift shaft walls and guide rails across different floors meant the lift cars could not travel smoothly. The centre of gravity for the lift cars was also imbalanced, and the overall workmanship quality was poor.

"A lift operating normally will experience a certain degree of minor displacement depending on the load conditions. However, if the clearance between the shaft wall and the lift car is insufficient, it can easily trigger the lift's safety devices, thereby causing the lift to stop operation," the report read.

As of Tuesday, rectification work had been completed on 18 lifts, seven of which were already in operation after passing inspections.

Repairs for the remaining lifts were expected to finish within this year.

The bureau added that ATAL Engineering Group, as the contractor, "bears overall responsibility" in ensuring the project is completed in accordance with requirements.

The report alleged that the firm was aware of dimension and verticality problems in the shaft, but "followed up sloppily" so the problems could not be addressed in a timely manner.

The Development Bureau will take disciplinary action against the contractor, as well as the subcontractor and consultancy firms.

This may include the suspension of tendering rights, downgrading or delisting.

"As the investigation discovered that the incident may involve other illegal activities, we have referred the matter to the relevant law enforcement authorities for further investigation," the report said.

It also said the Architectural Services Department failed to strictly adhere to internal guidelines when issuing the certificate of completion in January 2025.

"We have requested the director of architectural services to deal with the involved personnel appropriately in accordance with the Civil Service Regulations. The director of architectural services is currently liaising with the Civil Service Bureau to discuss the arrangements for initiating disciplinary proceedings," according to the document.

The Electrical and Mechanical Services Department was found to have complied with procedures in processing the applications for the lifts' operation permits, but "some personnel" did not conduct thorough investigations, and the department was urged to issue advisory letters to them, pointing out areas for improvement.

Officials will brief lawmakers at a Legco development panel meeting on Friday.

Edited by Edmond Fong

articles.title: Jensen Huang steps down as Nvidia CEO
articles.excerpt: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is stepping down, leaving the AI industry without its biggest champion and clouding the future of…
articles.fullText:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is stepping down, leaving the AI industry without its biggest champion and clouding the future of the chipmaker he built into an AI powerhouse.

Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress will take over as interim CEO as Nvidia looks for a permanent successor, the company said on Thursday.

It named former Synopsys CEO and board member Harvey Jones as its first-ever board chairman.

Huang, who co-founded Nvidia and is its fourth-largest investor with a stake of about 3.61 percent, will exit the board as well.

Nvidia shares fell more than 10 percent in premarket trading, and weighed on the broader market.

Pressure had been mounting on Huang in recent days after reports said the 63-year-old, who is married, had an affair with a Chinese businesswoman who US authorities suspect of spying for Beijing.

China has dismissed the spying allegations, calling them "baseless".

Nvidia's board met on Wednesday to consider his ouster, a person familiar with the matter said, after reports earlier in the day that Huang also had an extramarital affair with a senior company executive who reported to him.

Huang's exit plunges the US$4 trillion company into uncertainty and threatens to disrupt an AI ecosystem that he helped bankroll by pouring Nvidia's swelling cash pile back into cloud providers, suppliers and the industry's biggest labs.

"The risk is not that Nvidia suddenly loses its technology roadmap... that roadmap is largely visible for the next several years. The risk is execution. Jensen has been the chief conductor of an extraordinarily complex system," said Michael Feldman, portfolio manager at ClearBridge Investments.

"In a world with real bottlenecks, that coordination is a competitive advantage in itself."

Investor sentiment toward AI stocks has already been shaky as soaring cash burn and rising debt at traditionally cash-rich tech giants fuel doubts over whether the AI boom will pay off. (Reuters)

Edited by Edmond Fong

articles.title: Toll climbs in Brooklyn building collapse
articles.excerpt: At least eight people have died after a three-storey building in Brooklyn collapsed at the edge of a construction site…
articles.fullText:
At least eight people have died after a three-storey building in Brooklyn collapsed at the edge of a construction site, New York City’s mayor said on Thursday, as firefighters kept digging through the rubble to find others who may be trapped beneath the wreckage.

The building in the Flatbush neighbourhood of Brooklyn came down on Wednesday afternoon.

At least 17 people have been injured, including three firefighters, Mayor Zohran Mamdani said.

“There are no words for a loss of this magnitude,” Mamdani posted on X. “My heart is with the families and loved ones of those we have lost, those who are injured and everyone grieving today.”

Scores of firefighters and police officers wielding pickaxes and power saws clambered over the rubble pile overnight, punching holes through the ruins to pull dust-covered people from beneath piles of twisted wood and brick.

Rescuers used dogs to sniff for survivors. Firefighters used orange buckets as they removed debris from the rubble piles trying to reach people who may be trapped.

Heavy rain was forecast for the city on Thursday afternoon. It wasn't immediately known how that would affect search efforts.

The cause of the collapse was under investigation, but New York City’s buildings commissioner, Ahmed Tigani, noted that when the building fell, construction workers were excavating an empty lot next door for a new building.

Much of the rubble from the collapsed building – a mixed-use structure with apartments sitting atop ground-floor commercial space – wound up in a huge pile inside the construction pit. Another building that shared a wall with the collapsed structure remained standing, but its wall was shorn off, exposing the rooms inside, including a bedroom and closets filled with clothing.

About 250 firefighters were working the scene, Mamdani said. Two deaths were announced on Wednesday and the others were confirmed on Thursday.

On Wednesday night, firefighters pulled a woman – still alive and moving – out of a hole they had dug into the rubble pile, hoisting her up on a stretcher and rushing to a waiting ambulance. Additional people were pulled from beneath the pile as the night went on. (AP)

Edited by Edmond Fong

articles.title: The Download: COP31’s climate challenge and the quest for immortality
articles.excerpt: This is today’s edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in…
articles.fullText:
This is today’s edition of The Download , our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology.

What to know about this year’s UN climate talks

Thousands of delegates, lobbyists, and journalists have gathered in Antalya, Turkey, for COP31, the annual UN climate talks. But this year’s negotiations are taking place against a particularly tense geopolitical backdrop, as the world falls further behind the Paris Agreement’s goals.

Energy prices are soaring, and there are big questions about how countries will tackle the climate crisis. Expect a lot of back and forth on fossil fuels and climate finance, and whether negotiators can agree on meaningful action.

Here’s what you need to know about COP31 . 

—Casey Crownhart

This story is from The Spark, our weekly climate tech newsletter. Sign up to receive it in your inbox every Wednesday.

Inside the quest for cognitive immortality

Far-thinking technologists are working on ways to keep your brain going beyond death. MIT Technology Review’s latest Roundtables event explores their ideas, from gradual brain replacement to uploading memories to the cloud.

Join science editor Mary Beth Griggs and senior editor for biomedicine Antonio Regalado for this subscriber-only discussion.

Tune in live on Tuesday, November 17 at 5:00 p.m. GMT / 12:00 p.m. EST / 9:00 a.m. PST .

Want to join the conversation? Subscribe to MIT Technology Review for exclusive access to all our Roundtables.

The must-reads

I’ve combed the internet to find you today’s most fun/important/scary/fascinating stories about technology.

1 Nvidia is reportedly preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang
The board will meet as soon as today to determine his future. ( WSJ $)
+ Nvidia’s stock slid 8% after the report was published. ( BI )
+ Huang allegedly also had an affair with an Nvidia colleague. ( NYT $)
+ His exit could send shockwaves across the AI industry. ( Axios )
+ Stakes are high in AI’s trillion-dollar gamble. ( MIT Technology Review )

2 The Nvidia spy scandal is set to tighten chip exports
But Commerce Secretary Lutnick has stalled the curbs. ( CNBC )
+ China has signaled it will retaliate if they pass. ( FT $)
+ Chinese firms have started stockpiling Nvidia chips. ( Reuters $)
+ Democrats appear to be preparing an investigation. ( Politico )

3 A startup has built an AI to detect AI-made bioweapons
It runs offline on a laptop with a USB gene sequencer. ( Wired $)
+ Ukraine is opening up its battlefield data to train AI weapons. ( NYT $)
+ AI is making bioweapons easier to create. ( MIT Technology Review )

4 Anduril says its satellite can track spacecraft in orbital night
It uses an infrared sensor to detect hidden satellites. ( Ars Technica )
+ Anduril is also making smart glasses for warfare. ( MIT Technology Review )

articles.title: Carrick sacked by Man U, Sage out as Palace manager
articles.excerpt: Manchester United have dismissed manager Michael Carrick, the club said on Thursday, after a prolonged winless Premier League run culminated…
articles.fullText:
Manchester United have dismissed manager Michael Carrick, the club said on Thursday, after a prolonged winless Premier League run culminated in a 4-4 draw at home to Aston Villa last weekend, leaving the team mired in the relegation zone.

United have won only three of their 15 matches in all competitions under Carrick this season – including one league victory – leaving them 18th in the table on eight points after 10 games, one point from the bottom.

"After a disappointing start to the season, the club has come to the extremely difficult conclusion that a change is necessary in order to achieve our ambitions," United said in a statement on their website.

Carrick came under mounting pressure after a 3-0 home loss to Bournemouth and the former United midfielder carried the air of someone awaiting the inevitable after the defeat when fans chanted his name but booed the players off the pitch.

He had dropped captain Bruno Fernandes to the bench against Bournemouth and did not bring him on even when United were desperate for inspiration in midfield, but the struggling club gave Carrick another chance to revive their season.

Although he restored the playmaker to the starting lineup against Chelsea following clear-the-air talks and spoke of the team's determination to put things right, little changed as they were comprehensively outplayed in a 2-0 loss at Stamford Bridge.

A 3-2 comeback win over AS Roma in the Champions League briefly eased the pressure on Carrick, but United's familiar defensive frailties were exposed again in the 4-4 draw with Aston Villa, despite two injury-time goals salvaging a point.

Carrick is likely to be replaced by Mauricio Pochettino, the US men's national team coach, who has agreed to take over the newly-vacant post, according to reports in British media.

The former Southampton, Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea manager is one of the Premier League's most highly regarded former coaches.

Another struggling Premier League side, Crystal Palace, have also fired their manager.

Pierre Sage was let go on Thursday, bringing the Frenchman's five-month tenure to an end after a poor start to the season left the club bottom of the table.

Sage's departure followed a 3-1 home loss to Liverpool on Sunday, the south London club's fourth straight Premier League defeat. They are two points outside the safety zone.

"Crystal Palace Football Club can confirm that Pierre Sage has left his role as manager," Palace said in a statement.

"Three members of Pierre’s coaching staff – Jamal Alioui, Damien Della Santa and Sandy Guichard – have also left the club."

The 47-year-old, who managed Ligue 1 sides RC Lens and Olympique Lyonnais, took charge at Selhurst Park in June.

British media reports said former Tottenham Hotspur and Brentford manager Thomas Frank is the leading candidate to replace Sage. (Reuters)

articles.title: 'US uses spying claims as pretext for tech blockade'
articles.excerpt: China accused the United States on Thursday of using spurious spying claims as a pretext to impose a technological "blockade"…
articles.fullText:
China accused the United States on Thursday of using spurious spying claims as a pretext to impose a technological "blockade" on Beijing, following claims that Nvidia boss Jensen Huang was the victim of a Chinese espionage plot.

"China's technological progress is driven by independent innovation and open cooperation. The US side should stop fabricating such 'spy' narratives as a pretext for imposing a technological blockade," Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning told a regular briefing.

Huang, who co-founded Nvidia and turned it into the world's leading supplier of the chips that power AI, has admitted to having an extramarital affair.

China has dismissed the claims about spying on Huang as "groundless speculation" and "an attempt to smear China".

The furore comes ahead of a meeting next week between President Xi Jinping and his US counterpart Donald Trump at the Apec summit in Shenzhen. (AFP)

Edited by Edmond Fong

articles.title: Ex-in-law 'followed dad's orders after Choi killing'
articles.excerpt: The former brother-in-law of celebrity Abby Choi told the High Court on Thursday that he should have called the police…
articles.fullText:
The former brother-in-law of celebrity Abby Choi told the High Court on Thursday that he should have called the police or an ambulance on the day of her killing.

This came a day after he told the court that it was his brother – Choi’s ex-husband – who killed her.

On the 36th day of the trial, Kwong Kong-kit said he should have been braver and more rational.

He told the court that after he drove the car to the Tai Mei Tuk carpark in Tai Po, he saw Choi lying on the floor of the car with no sound or movement coming from her.

Kwong said he followed instructions given by his father, Kwong Kau, in a subsequent call to drive the car to the Lung Mei Village.

He parked it next to his father’s car when he got there.

Kwong said it was about 20 minutes between when Choi was attacked by his brother and when they arrived at the village house, saying his mind went blank during the period.

Kwong also said he believed Choi might already have been dead as she was unresponsive.

He said his father put Choi into a plastic box after wrapping her body in a blanket.

His father then instructed him to carry the box into the house before telling him and his brother to leave, Kwong said.

Kwong Kong-kit, Choi's former husband Kwong Kong-chi and former father-in-law Kwong Kau were charged with murdering her on February 21, 2023, at Lung Mei Village in Tai Po and preventing the lawful burial of her body.

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: HK, region take toll as Nvidia fate hangs in balance
articles.excerpt: Asian shares and US futures declined on Thursday as concerns over leadership at chipmaker Nvidia weighed on artificial intelligence-related stocks…
articles.fullText:
Asian shares and US futures declined on Thursday as concerns over leadership at chipmaker Nvidia weighed on artificial intelligence-related stocks.

In Hong Kong, the benchmark Hang Seng Index closed down 307 points, or 1.3 percent, to 24,008 on turnover of HK$202.65 billion.

The tech index plunged 95 points, or 2.4 percent, to 3,931 while the China enterprises index fell 114 points, or 1.4 percent, to 8,056.

Up north, the benchmark Shanghai Composite Index ended down 24 points, or 0.67 percent, at 3,655.

The Shenzhen Component Index fell 191 points, or 1.68 percent, to 11,197 while the ChiNext Index dived 62 points, or 2.44 percent, to 2,509.

In after-hours trading, Nvidia’s shares fell 8.6 percent after reports said Nvidia’s board was meeting late on Wednesday to discuss the situation surrounding its chief executive, Jensen Huang and his extramarital affairs.

Nvidia's shares climbed 2.9 percent on Wednesday.

Its shares have fallen after the company said it was investigating Huang, who has admitted to being unfaithful to his wife.

The New York Times reported on Wednesday that Huang was involved in a second extramarital affair.

The tech company's board was preparing to meet as soon as Wednesday to determine Huang's future, according to the Wall Street Journal, which quoted people familiar with the matter.

Huang has built Nvidia to be one of the world's biggest and most important companies, designing advanced chips crucial to the AI buildout that has helped drive stock markets to record highs and boosted economies around the world.

"Nvidia has spent years convincing investors that it is one of the most important companies in the AI revolution," wrote Charu Chanana at Saxo Markets.

"Now, the biggest question surrounding the company is not about its chips, competitors or earnings. It is about its founder."

She said Huang was key to the firm's future, including dealings with governments.

"Nvidia's technological advantage would not disappear with his departure," she added.

"Its CUDA software ecosystem, product capabilities and customer relationships remain formidable strengths.

"But an abrupt exit without a credible succession plan could force investors to reassess how much of Nvidia's future depends on Huang personally."

In Tokyo, the Nikkei reversed early gains to end 429 points, or 0.7 percent, lower at 60,819 amid reports that a potential sacking was in the offing at Nvidia for its founder, Jensen Huang.

The broader Topix edged up almost eight points, or 0.2 percent, at 3,937.

In Seoul, the Nvidia reports also took its toll on the Kospi, sending it down 32 points, or 0.61 percent, to 5,342. (Agencies)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Xi urges nation to carry on Sun's revolutionary legacy
articles.excerpt: President Xi Jinping on Thursday called for carrying forward the legacy of Sun Yat-sen, one of the nation's revered revolutionary…
articles.fullText:
President Xi Jinping on Thursday called for carrying forward the legacy of Sun Yat-sen, one of the nation's revered revolutionary forefathers, to make joint efforts for national rejuvenation and turn into reality the great dream of all Chinese people since the advent of modern times.

Xi, who is also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the remarks at a gathering held in Beijing to commemorate the 160th anniversary of Sun's birth.

Born in 1866, Sun led the revolution of 1911 more than a century ago to abolish the absolute monarchy that had ruled China for thousands of years. Sun died in 1925.

Addressing the event in the Great Hall of the People, Xi hailed Sun as a great national hero, a great patriot and a great pioneer of China's democratic revolution.

He noted that Chinese communists are the most steadfast supporters, loyal collaborators and faithful successors to the revolutionary cause initiated by Sun.

For more than 100 years, the party has led the Chinese people in writing the most magnificent chapter in the history of the Chinese nation, Xi said.

"The best way for us to remember Dr Sun is to emulate, inherit and carry forward his invaluable spirit, steadily advancing our endeavors to build a great country and rejuvenate our nation," he said.

Xi also called on people on both sides of the Taiwan Strait and Chinese around the world to contribute to the peaceful development of cross-strait relations and complete the country's reunification.

Resolving the Taiwan question and realising the country’s complete reunification is an unswerving historical mission for the Communist Party of China, a shared aspiration of all Chinese people, and a requirement for realising the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, Xi said. (Xinhua)

Edited by Aaron Tam

articles.title: Apec to spotlight Shenzhen's global fintech push
articles.excerpt: Shenzhen’s financial services sector has been increasingly shaped by the deep integration of fintech and by its expanding overseas reach…
articles.fullText:
Shenzhen’s financial services sector has been increasingly shaped by the deep integration of fintech and by its expanding overseas reach, according to a senior executive at Ping An Property and Casualty Insurance Company.

Those trends are likely to draw wider attention next week, when global leaders arrive in the southern Chinese city for the Apec summit.

Xu Hua, assistant president of Ping An Property and Casualty Insurance Company, said the company’s own history mirrors Shenzhen's fintech development.

Founded in the 1980s in Shekou – an industrial area in western Shenzhen – it has grown from a regional insurer into a service network covering more than 110 countries.

Financial services already form one of Shenzhen’s four pillar industries. Ping An Property and Casualty Insurance Company is among the companies taking part in the meeting, and its parent, Ping An Group, is one of the official sponsors.

Xu said Shenzhen’s financial industry is most characterised by the deep integration of finance and technology.

"Shenzhen is an innovation capital. It brings together a group of representative technology companies. Technological innovation comes with trial and error and risk. It faces practical difficulties such as high research and development investment, rapid technology iteration and strong uncertainty," he said.

"Wherever innovation goes, insurance must follow. Overall, technology is Shenzhen’s underlying character. What insurance needs to do is serve well as a shock absorber for the real economy, so that technology companies dare to innovate, dare to invest and dare to go global."

Xu said the company has tailor-made more than 400 million yuan in dedicated risk protection for this summit.

He believes the meeting will not only bring short-term benefits, but also have long-term value, and hopes that the exchange opportunities at the Apec meeting can be transformed into sustained project cooperation.

For cross-border operations, he called for closer cooperation with insurers, reinsurers and professional service providers so that companies can better understand local risks and coverage requirements.

In sectors such as new energy, advanced manufacturing and the digital economy, he proposed that industry partners jointly assess emerging risks and develop products that keep pace with innovation.

Xu said that in addition to helping mainland enterprises go global and providing protection services for their overseas expansion, the company has also formed close ties with Apec economies.

The sector’s scale underscores its role in the city: financial services account for nearly 15 percent of Shenzhen’s GDP, and the Shenzhen Stock Exchange had more than 2,900 listed companies as of the end of September.

Edited by Aaron Tam

articles.title: CE hails spirits of national rejuvenation
articles.excerpt: Chief Executive John Lee on Thursday said the SAR government was working to enrich resources for patriotic education, providing a…
articles.fullText:
Chief Executive John Lee on Thursday said the SAR government was working to enrich resources for patriotic education, providing a broader platform for the younger generation to learn about national affairs.

Speaking at a ceremony to commemorate the 160th anniversary of the birthday of Sun Yat-sen, Lee said the national hero had deep ties with Hong Kong – the birthplace of his revolutionary ideas.

The best way to commemorate Sun is to carry forward his spirit of revitalising the nation, he said, adding that the city’s first five-year plan had proposed to step up patriotic education.

“The SAR government attaches great importance to patriotic education, and is making continuous efforts to promote mainstream values centred on the affection for our country and Hong Kong and in conformity with the ‘One Country, Two Systems’ principle to strengthen people’s sense of identity with the country and Chinese culture, enhance national confidence and pride, and foster a conscious commitment to upholding national unity and solidarity,” Lee said.

The CE went on to say that the SAR government would continue to host mainland study tours for students while supporting non-governmental organisations in hosting youth exchange programmes, so that youngsters in the city could experience firsthand the nation’s history, culture, and latest developments.

He urged people to make contributions to the country’s development and the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

Edited by Tony Sabine

Asian stocks wobbled at the start of regional trading on Thursday, while Nvidia shares plunged in after-hours trading on news that its board may oust longtime chief executive Jensen Huang.

In Hong Kong, the benchmark Hang Seng Index opened down 194 points, or 0.8 percent, at 24,121.

The tech index fell 32 points, or 0.8 percent, to 3,995 while the China Enterprises Index slipped 66 points, or 0.81 percent, to 8,105.

On the mainland, the Shanghai Composite Index inched down seven points, or 0.21 percent, to open at 3,673.

The Shenzhen Component Index was 28 points, or 0.25 percent, lower at 11,361 while the ChiNext Index was down 0.5 percent at 2,559.

Nvidia's board is meeting late on Wednesday to decide whether to oust Huang, a source said, as the world's dominant supplier of AI processors grapples with the fallout of allegations that he had an affair with a suspected spy for China.

The New York Times has also reported that Huang had had an affair with a company executive who reported to him.

"It looks bad from every single angle," said Jake Dollarhide, chief executive at Longbow Asset Management in Tulsa, Oklahoma.

"I believe the board won't oust him until they have an all-star, a known entity in the tech sector, to replace him. At the end of the day, let's not forget that the Nvidia chip is the centrepiece of the AI story."

Shares in Nvidia slid more than eight percent after the bell, weighing on S&P 500 e-mini futures, which slipped 0.4 percent.

In Tokyo, the Nikkei opened 226 points, or 0.37 percent, higher at 61,475 and was 390 points higher still at one stage before noon.

In Seoul, the Kospi opened 10 points, or 0.2 percent, at 5,385 and, like the Nikkei, tracked up cautiously by 38 points at one stage before lunch.

"Renewed optimism around AI drove US equities higher overnight, with positive developments around CoreWeave and Anthropic adding to enthusiasm around the sector and helping the S&P 500 and Nasdaq rally," Westpac analysts wrote in a note. (Agencies)

articles.title: Andreeva stuns Sabalenka to reach WTA Finals last four
articles.excerpt: French Open champion Mirra Andreeva stormed past Aryna Sabalenka 6-4, 6-0 to reach the last four of the WTA Finals…
articles.fullText:
French Open champion Mirra Andreeva stormed past Aryna Sabalenka 6-4, 6-0 to reach the last four of the WTA Finals on Wednesday as Elina Svitolina kept her bid on track with a three-set win over Karolina Muchova.

Russian 19-year-old Andreeva held her nerve after falling behind 4-1 in the opening set, winning the last 11 games to seal the round-robin victory in just 62 minutes.

"Oh my God, I'm even happier than I was after my first match," Andreeva said. "I feel like I can play another two matches, I'm so full of energy. I'm so pumped up. I'm so happy."

Andreeva, whose three titles this year include her maiden major at Roland Garros, is making her singles debut in the elite season-ending event.

The world number three seemed to be feeling the nerves in the early going against second-ranked Sabalenka.

Irked that she had given up a break with a double fault, she was able to flip the switch, dealing handily with Sabalenka's big serves and pushing the Belarusian star back with her own big groundstrokes.

Andreeva crucially kept momentum on her side with a break for a 3-0 lead in the second set.

Sabalenka, trailing 0-40, saved three break points, but Andreeva gave herself another with a swinging volley winner and grabbed another break when a Sabalenka forehand flew just long.

The increasingly demoralised Sabalenka had no answer. After the Belarusian smacked a backhand into the net to give her opponent match point Andreeva polished things off with a service winner.

It was another disappointing performance for the 28-year-old Sabalenka, whose three wins this season include prestigious back-to-back victories at Indian Wells and Miami but no Grand Slams.

Making her sixth straight Finals appearance, Sabalenka can still advance if she beats Svitolina in their final round-robin match on Friday.

Svitolina roared back from a set down to beat Muchova 3-6, 6-2, 6-2.

Ukrainian veteran Svitolina lifted the WTA Finals trophy in 2018 but hadn't been back to the elite season-ending event since 2019.

She got off to a rocky start against Muchova, who broke Svitolina three times in the opening set.

Trailing 2-1 on serve in the second Svitolina found her range, winning five straight games to force a third set.

"I was not happy with the first set," Svitolina said. "I didn't play as well. I just made some adjustments, tactical adjustments.

"I think it helped me also to be more aggressive, because I was too passive in the first set," Svitolina said.

Muchova's second round-robin defeat coupled with Andreeva's victory means the Czech was eliminated from semi-final contention. (AFP)

Edited by Nazvi Careem

articles.title: Nvidia preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang: WSJ
articles.excerpt: Nvidia's board is preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang after he had two extramarital affairs, the Wall Street Journal reported…
articles.fullText:
Nvidia's board is preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang after he had two extramarital affairs, the Wall Street Journal reported on Wednesday, citing people familiar with the matter.

The board is preparing to meet as soon as Wednesday to determine his future, the report added.

Huang's potential departure would leave a leadership vacuum at the roughly US$4 trillion chipmaker he co-founded and built over more than three decades to become the dominant supplier of AI chips at the centre of the global artificial-intelligence boom.

The company's shares slid about 8 percent in after-hours trading. Including Wednesday's after-hours selloff, Nvidia has lost about US$600 billion in stock market value this week since the board announced its investigation.

"Huang being removed immediately could be challenging for Nvidia since it does not have a succession plan in place... If Mr Huang broke the law or violated company policies, the board is likely to act as soon as they have proof," Gil Luria, head of technology research at DA Davidson, said.

Earlier in the day, the New York Times reported that Huang had an extramarital affair with a company executive who reported to him.

The relationship was with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's vice president of healthcare, the New York Times said, citing five people who worked at the company.

When reached by phone on Wednesday and asked about his relationship with Powell, Huang said, "I don't think you should be talking to me directly." He then hung up, the New York Times reported.

Nvidia and Powell did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Reuters could not immediately verify the reports.

The reports mark a sharp escalation in a controversy that began with revelations about Huang's relationship with Alice Huang, a woman US intelligence has said was involved in facilitating shipments of Nvidia chips to Chinese firms.

Beijing has dismissed allegations that Alice Huang was a spy for China as "groundless speculation".

In a memo to employees on Sunday, Huang acknowledged being unfaithful to his wife and took "full responsibility," but gave no details about the relationship.

The same day, Nvidia's board launched an investigation into whether Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. The probe is being overseen by independent directors with outside legal counsel. At the time, the board expressed confidence in Huang.

US President Donald Trump has said he had not discussed the allegations with Huang but voiced support for the Nvidia chief, calling him "an honourable guy" who had "done an amazing job for our country."

Huang faces a potential congressional subpoena if he doesn't respond to a request to provide a closed-door briefing about the allegations that he had a close relationship with the Chinese businesswoman.

Huang co-founded Nvidia in 1993 with Curtis Priem and Chris Malachowsky. Its early hits were graphics chips for computer games, before its CUDA software opened the processors to general computing and, later, AI. (Reuters)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Kane says England record a 'testament to dedication'
articles.excerpt: England captain Harry Kane said breaking the Three Lions' appearance record in Thursday's Nations League clash with Croatia will represent…
articles.fullText:
England captain Harry Kane said breaking the Three Lions' appearance record in Thursday's Nations League clash with Croatia will represent a "testament to all the dedication" that has gone into his career.

When Kane leads England out at Wembley to win his 126th cap, he will surpass the previous record held since 1990 by former goalkeeper Peter Shilton.

It will be the latest landmark in an incredible 12 months for the Bayern Munich striker, who in October became the first English player in 25 years to win the Ballon d'Or.

The 33-year-old Kane is also England's record scorer with 91 goals.

"It's definitely up there as the biggest (achievement)," Kane told reporters on Wednesday.

"I think it showcases consistency at the highest level. Testament to all the dedication, the time people don't see that keeps me fit and healthy. This is one of the biggest milestones in my career."

Since leaving Tottenham to join Bayern in 2023, Kane has taken his game to another level.

Aside from scoring 156 goals for the German club, he has also finally laid a ghost to rest in winning the first silverware of his career, including Bundesliga titles in 2025 and 2026.

However, England have not won a major tournament since winning the 1966 World Cup on home soil.

Kane suffered fresh frustration in July as he lost in a World Cup semi-final for the second time when Argentina came from behind to beat England.

Kane said he hoped there was enough left in his legs for another tilt at the World Cup in 2030.

"In terms of what's next, I don't like to put limits – 100 goals (for England) is a milestone to reach as soon as possible," said Kane.

"We've done extremely well in tournaments, going into latter stages.

"I'm feeling really good and hopefully there will be many more years to see what I can achieve."

Other near-misses with Kane for England include two losses in European Championship finals, in 2021 on penalties to Italy and then in 2024 to Spain.

But he went on to win his first trophy with Bayern the following season.

Kane said, despite the perpetual disappointments, he kept believing one day his luck would change in terms of silverware.

"Obviously after any big loss, especially a final, you look into everything, you try and analyse it," he said.

"I don't think I ever doubted that it would come." (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Man U reach verbal agreement with Pochettino: reports
articles.excerpt: Manchester United have reportedly reached a "verbal agreement in principle" with Mauricio Pochettino to replace Michael Carrick as their manager…
articles.fullText:
Manchester United have reportedly reached a "verbal agreement in principle" with Mauricio Pochettino to replace Michael Carrick as their manager in a bid to revive the fortunes of the struggling English giants.

Carrick's position at Old Trafford has been the subject of intense speculation following United's worst start to a season in 40 years, leaving them languishing in the Premier League relegation zone after an eight-match winless run.

He remains in post but it is believed Carrick's future will be decided at a meeting attended by influential shareholder Jim Ratcliffe, chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox in Monaco on Wednesday.

Berrada and Wilcox are reportedly leaning towards dismissing Carrick.

United States head coach Pochettino has extensive experience of the Premier League following spells in charge of Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea.

It was only three months ago, however, that Pochettino signed a contract extension to remain with the United States through to the 2030 World Cup.

US Soccer would be due compensation should he move to Manchester, with the 54-year-old understood to have a £7.5 million release clause.

But Sky Sports reported Wednesday that United have "reached a verbal agreement in principle" with Pochettino, linked with a move to Old Trafford on several previous occasions, to become their new head coach.

Carrick was seen arriving at United's Carrington training ground on Wednesday but it appears to be only a matter of time before his turbulent reign comes to an end.

The 45-year-old had been granted a stay of execution after he was widely expected to be axed in late October following a 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth.

But United were beaten 2-0 at Chelsea, then scrambled a last-gasp 3-2 win against Roma in the Champions League after falling two goals down.

It appeared former United and England midfielder Carrick would be on the way out when his team twice trailed Aston Villa by two goals on Sunday.

When United scored twice in stoppage-time to rescue an improbable 4-4 draw, it was interpreted as a positive sign for Carrick as the players were still fighting for him.

But a change now appears likely, with former Newcastle manager Eddie Howe, ex-Chelsea chief Antonio Conte and former Germany coach Julian Nagelsmann also linked with the United job.

United have the rest of the two-week international break to resolve their managerial situation before returning to action at bitter rivals Liverpool on November 22.

Carrick has presided over United's slide to 18th place, their lowest position 10 games into a top-flight season since 1986/87 when they were 20th.

He was hired on a permanent basis in the close-season after leading United to a third-place finish in the Premier League during his spell as interim boss.

Carrick had won plaudits for steadying the ship after Ruben Amorim's volatile reign ended in the sack in January.

But, hampered by the club's underwhelming recruitment in the transfer window, Carrick's team have endured a steep decline this term.

United, who have not won the title since Alex Ferguson's final season as boss in 2012/13, only signed midfielders Youri Tielemans, Carlos Baleba and Andrey Santos in the summer transfer window despite the glaring need for new forwards.

Carrick has struggled to maintain discipline among his squad, dropping captain Bruno Fernandes after he criticised his manager's tactics during a 4-1 thrashing at Champions League debutants Como.

He also axed Lisandro Martinez after the United defender criticised the club's hierarchy for their lack of top-quality signings.

United fans have remained largely supportive of Carrick, focusing their anger on majority owners the Glazer family, Ratcliffe and the under-achieving players. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: CoreWeave results lift tech stocks as dollar gains
articles.excerpt: Stock markets rose on Wednesday on renewed optimism over AI following strong results from data centre operator CoreWeave, while the…
articles.fullText:
Stock markets rose on Wednesday on renewed optimism over AI following strong results from data centre operator CoreWeave, while the dollar extended a rally on expectations for at least one more Federal Reserve interest rate hike.

Wall Street's main indices enjoyed a buoyant session led by the tech-heavy Nasdaq, which finished up 1.6 percent.

"The primary catalyst for the upside action is, ironically, one of the primary catalysts for the downside action that had been seen in the AI trade," said Briefing.com analyst Patrick O'Hare.

"That would be CoreWeave, which posted better-than-feared third-quarter results and issued a reassuring outlook that has quieted some of the debt financing concerns surrounding its AI buildout plans," he added.

CoreWeave said sales would come in at US$13-US$13.3 billion this year, beating estimates and soothing worries about its ability to finance its heavy debt burden, which fuelled a sharp sell-off last month.

Shares in CoreWeave surged nearly 25 percent.

"This relief trade is carrying across the AI trade complex to include hardware, software, and semiconductor stocks," said O'Hare.

The gains in US equities came despite signalling from US central bankers that the Fed will lift interest rates in December to address persistent inflation. The US dollar rose to its highest level since May 2025 after one top Fed official floated the idea of a 0.5 percentage point interest rate increase next month.

After last week's rout fuelled by fears that Democrats would ramp up regulation of AI, tech stocks have bounced this week on bargain-buying and hopes that fears may have been overdone.

"Overall, the market is putting AI doubts to one side and is focusing on revenue potential and mega cap IPO as we move through this week," said Kathleen Brooks, research director at XTB.

Semiconductor companies advanced, including scandal-plagued Nvidia, which bounced 3 percent after a two-day rout following the bombshell revelation of an affair between CEO Jensen Huang and a woman suspected of being a spy. The firm is now the subject of an FBI investigation.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 254 points, or 0.5 percent, to 52,486, the S&P 500 gained 98 points, or 1.3 percent, to 7,619 and the Nasdaq Composite gained 400 points, or 1.6percent, to 25,466.

Oil prices advanced after sinking on Tuesday on hopes for a US-Iran agreement to end their war and reopen the crucial Strait of Hormuz. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Wang Yi holds 'positive, constructive' call with Rubio
articles.excerpt: Foreign Minister Wang Yi held a "positive and constructive" call with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Wednesday, Xinhua…
articles.fullText:
Foreign Minister Wang Yi held a "positive and constructive" call with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Wednesday, Xinhua news agency reported, with Beijing expressing willingness to strengthen communication and cooperation with Washington.

The talks come roughly a week ahead of the Apec Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, where Presidents Xi Jinping and Donald Trump are expected to meet.

The current stability in China-US relations has not come easily, Wang said, calling it "a rational choice made by the two major countries based on respective and shared interests," the Xinhua report said.

The Xinhua report quoted Wang as saying that China, having maintained a stable and consistent policy towards the United States, is willing to strengthen communication and cooperation with Washington, properly handle differences and sensitive issues, support each other in hosting the 2026 Apec Economic Leaders' Meeting and the G20 Summit, and work to bring a constructive China-US relationship of strategic stability into effect and deliver results.

Xi and Trump have met twice already this year and Rubio told reporters on Tuesday there was work underway to arrange a trilateral meeting on the Apec sidelines involving Xi, Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin.

Rubio said Trump wants that meeting to happen and added: "We think it should be possible."

Trump said on Sunday he thought he would meet Xi and Putin in Shenzhen and discuss ending the war in Iran and denuclearisation.

He said in October that he was open to three-way arms control talks with Xi and Putin, which he said would focus on nuclear weapons.

China's foreign ministry said last month that its "nuclear strength is by no means at the same level with that of the US and Russia" and that it would be "neither fair, reasonable nor realistic to ask China to join the so-called trilateral nuclear disarmament negotiations at this stage."

The Wall Street Journal has reported that Putin has pitched using a trilateral meeting to discuss an end to Russia's long-running war in Ukraine. (Xinhua/Reuters)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: What to know about this year’s UN climate talks
articles.excerpt: It’s that time of year again: Thousands of delegates, lobbyists, and journalists are gathered for the annual UN climate talks…
articles.fullText:
It’s that time of year again: Thousands of delegates, lobbyists, and journalists are gathered for the annual UN climate talks, taking place this time in Antalya, Turkey.

COP31 officially kicked off on November 8, marking the beginning of negotiations on one of the biggest stages of the climate world. Turkey and Australia are cohosting this year’s talks, which are scheduled to wrap up on November 20.

This annual gathering can often serve as an indicator of where the world stands on addressing and adapting to the climate crisis. And this year’s talks are sure to be a doozy—expect a lot of back and forth on fossil fuels and climate finance in particular. Here’s what you should know about COP31.

In recent years, the tension always feels high when COP rolls around. (COP stands for “Conference of the Parties.”) But this year feels especially charged: The world is still grappling with the ongoing war in Iran, which has disrupted the Middle East and sent economic shock waves around the world as energy prices have spiked.

This year’s COP will be the second without a formal delegation from the US. President Trump formally withdrew the country from the Paris Agreement earlier this year and is in the process of withdrawing from the UN Framework Committee on Climate Change. That’s the treaty that allows formal participation in negotiations.

Meanwhile, things aren’t looking good for the Paris Agreement, which was established at UN climate talks 11 years ago, setting a goal of limiting warming to 1.5 °C over preindustrial levels. In a report published in September, the UN Environment Program acknowledged that global warming is set to exceed that 1.5 °C goal, “likely within the next few years.”

So as climate talks kick off, there’s an obvious, urgent question looming about how to quickly cut emissions to limit warming. There’s also the major issue of how to pay for efforts to address emissions and to help a warming world endure the inevitable damage.

Two years ago, talks ended in a goal of mobilizing $300 billion per year by 2035 to help pay to reduce emissions and adapt to climate change. (Rich nations provided $136.7 billion in 2024, according to the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development. ) And last year, the COP30 agreement included a goal of tripling the money for adaptation over that period. (Such funding has been quite flat over the past few years.)

The world got a tragic reminder of just how high the stakes are earlier this year, when a glacier collapse caused devastating flooding in the Himalayas. The flood killed approximately 1,500 people, left over 5,000 missing, and caused nearly $5 billion in damage. The UN loss and damages fund committed $20 million to helping Nepal recover (less than 1% of the total estimated cost to the country).

Another key trend to watch is how the formal negotiations engage with the topic of fossil fuels. Three years ago, the final agreement text explicitly called for a transition away from them. But it felt as if things took a step back last year, when the final agreement didn’t even mention the phrase “fossil fuels” once. This will be an interesting conversation, especially because cohosts Turkey and Australia have both faced criticism over their relationships with these fuels—Australia is a major exporter of coal and natural gas, and Turkey’s grid relies heavily on fossil fuels, including coal.

Outside the formal negotiations, COP31 president Murat Kurum, Turkey’s environment minister, is spearheading a side agenda, including two informal initiatives that will be worth watching. These wouldn’t be part of the official agreement text, but countries could sign on to signal support.

One is a pledge to make AI more sustainable; this is almost comically squishy, even as voluntary COP pledges go. The text includes explicit wording that it creates no new obligations for countries, so don’t expect anything resembling enforcement there.

The COP leadership is also pushing to make electricity a larger part of member countries’ energy use. Today, only about 23% of global energy is used in the form of electricity. Fossil fuels, like gasoline in vehicles or natural gas for heating, make up the bulk of the rest. Shifting to more electricity use, and relying on cleaner sources for that electricity, could help drive down emissions. The new pledge’s target is for electricity to make up 35% of total energy consumption by 2035.

With leadership billing this as an “implementation COP,” it would be great to see some real, tangible progress on the global challenge of addressing climate change. I’m not expecting anything groundbreaking, but we’ll be tuned in to see what the final agreement shapes up to be.

This article is from The Spark, MIT Technology Review ’s weekly climate newsletter. To receive it in your inbox every Wednesday, sign up here .

articles.title: Dr Sun Yat-sen exhibition to be held
articles.excerpt: The Dr Sun Yat-sen Museum will present the " Timeless Impressions - The Shaping and Representation of Dr Sun Yat-sen's…
articles.fullText:
The Dr Sun Yat-sen Museum will present the " Timeless Impressions - The Shaping and Representation of Dr Sun Yat-sen's Images " exhibition from November 13.

This year marks the 160th anniversary of the birth of Dr Sun Yat-sen; the exhibition features over 80 pieces of artefacts associated with Dr Sun's image.

Addressing the opening ceremony today, the Assistant Director (Heritage and Museums) of Leisure and Cultural Services, Ng Chi-wo, said Dr Sun dedicated his entire life to the revolutionary cause: from resolving to save the nation and devoting himself to his studies, to organising the revolution and overthrowing the imperial system, and devoting his life to revitalising China. The ideas and strategies he put forward laid the blueprint for the modernisation of China, and his achievements made enduring contributions to social progress and the well-being of the people.

He added that the ideals advocated by Dr Sun, including equality, fraternity and "the world is for all", together with his vision of "revitalising China", are subtly instilling his spirit into our hearts through various forms that permeate our daily lives imperceptibly.

Dr Sun lived during an era marked by the rapid development of photographic technology and print media, and his image as a revolutionary was widely disseminated across the country through pictures and text. The exhibition features coins and stamps bearing his likeness that circulated nationwide, along with commemorative philatelic items, sculptures and cartoons from China and abroad.

It also showcases around 100 historical photographs, newspaper clippings, and archival materials, together with multimedia presentations, to illustrate how the multifaceted images of Dr Sun - patriotic yet well-versed in both Chinese and Western learning - have been shaped and represented through pictures, texts, physical objects and public spaces in different periods, offering a retrospective of his illustrious life.

There will be a series of free experiential activities including thematic lectures, exhibition guided tours for the public and school groups, and workshops, as well as panel exhibitions and parent-child workshops at six public libraries.

Jointly organised by the Dr Sun Yat-sen Museum and the Sun Yat-sen Research Projects of the Department of History of the Hong Kong Baptist University, the exhibition will be held until July 7 next year, with free admission.

articles.title: Teacher certificate bill proposed
articles.excerpt: The Education Bureau has proposed amending the law to enhance the teacher registration mechanism by introducing practising certificate requirements, thereby…
articles.fullText:
The Education Bureau has proposed amending the law to enhance the teacher registration mechanism by introducing practising certificate requirements, thereby upholding the professionalism of the teaching force. The Government will publish the Education (Amendment) Bill 2026 in the Gazette tomorrow and introduce it to the Legislative Council for first and second readings on November 25.

The bureau noted that it has referenced teacher registration systems in various jurisdictions alongside the registration and practising certificate requirements of other Hong Kong professions. It stated that making a practising certificate a prerequisite for teaching, in addition to the existing statutory registration, could elevate public recognition of the sector and raise the social status of teachers.

The bill will establish statutory rules requiring all teachers and principals of publicly funded schools, private schools, international schools and kindergartens to hold both teacher registration and practising certificates. Each practising certificate will remain valid for a maximum of three school years.

To ensure educators keep abreast of the latest global and local educational policies, teachers must meet a mandatory continuing professional development requirement to obtain a practising certificate. This measure aims to align their knowledge and pedagogy with the evolving needs of students and society.

The bureau pointed out that as role models and key figures in nurturing young people, teachers have a profound impact on students through their conduct, values, words and deeds. Amid rapid societal changes, parents and the wider public hold increasingly high expectations for teacher professionalism.

The bureau highlighted that the bill addresses the practical operational needs of schools, encourages educators to keep pace with the times and strengthens staff management to safeguard student well-being. It also establishes safeguards to bar individuals convicted of offences endangering national security from teaching, protecting students while upholding professional integrity and public confidence.

Click here for details.

articles.title: Tai Po fire civil claims notes issued
articles.excerpt: The Judiciary issued two Special Practice Notes today on handling civil claims arising from the Tai Po Wang Fuk Court…
articles.fullText:
The Judiciary issued two Special Practice Notes today on handling civil claims arising from the Tai Po Wang Fuk Court fire, seeking to ensure a fair and proportionate allocation of judicial resources without impairing access to courts or a fair trial. Taking into account the extensive casualties and severe damage caused by the fire, the Judiciary anticipates a large number of claims involving complex issues and substantial sums will soon be brought before the courts.

Given the time, costs and uncertainties involved in litigation, the Judiciary noted it is in the interests of both the parties and the public to resolve these claims initially through without-prejudice negotiations. Failing that, parties should pursue alternative dispute resolution (ADR) such as mediation, leaving litigation as a last resort.

Taking immediate effect, the two Special Practice Notes direct parties to attempt resolving their fire-related disputes via ADR both before and after proceedings commence. They also establish special expedited court procedures aimed at settling claims fairly, quickly and at a reasonable cost.

The first Special Practice Note covers all civil claims arising from the fire, excluding certain specified categories, which are handled by the High Court or the District Court. The second covers employees' compensation claims handled by the District Court, alongside civil claims handled by the Small Claims Tribunal or the Labour Tribunal.

Members of the public can also access various free legal services in Hong Kong, including the Free Legal Advice Scheme . Meanwhile, the Judiciary has launched a dedicated webpage offering one-stop information on mediation for civil claims linked to the incident.

articles.title: 3 sports events get ‘M’ Mark status
